name: 46 , xx testicular disorders of sex development
query: Query: 46 , xx testicular disorders of sex development [SEP] Xx testicular disorders of sex development 46 is congenital conditions in individuals in which male gonads develop in a genetic female (female to male sex reversal).

name: abdomen , acute
query: Query: abdomen , acute [SEP] Acute abdomen is a clinical syndrome with acute abdominal pain that is severe, localized, and rapid in onset. Acute abdomen may be caused by a variety of disorders, injuries, or diseases.

name: abdominal wall
query: Query: abdominal wall [SEP] Abdominal wall is the outer margins of the abdomen, extending from the osteocartilaginous thoracic cage to the pelvis. Though its major part is muscular, the abdominal wall consists of at least seven layers: the skin, subcutaneous fat, deep fascia; abdominal muscles, transversalis fascia, extraperitoneal fat, and the parietal peritoneum.

name: abortion , incomplete
query: Query: abortion , incomplete [SEP] Incomplete abortion is premature loss of pregnancy in which not all the products of conception have been expelled.

name: abortion , threatened
query: Query: abortion , threatened [SEP] Threatened abortion is uterine bleeding from a gestation of less than 20 weeks without any cervical dilatation. It is characterized by vaginal bleeding, lower back discomfort, or midline pelvic cramping and a risk factor for miscarriage.

name: abstracts
query: Query: abstracts [SEP] Abstracts is works consisting of lists of publications on a subject and that provide full annotated bibliographical information together with substantive summaries or condensations of the facts, ideas, or opinions presented in each publication listed. (From lc Subject Cataloging Manual)

name: acceleration
query: Query: acceleration [SEP] Acceleration is an increase in the rate of speed.

name: acetylcholine release inhibitors
query: Query: acetylcholine release inhibitors [SEP] Acetylcholine release inhibitors is compounds that block release of the neurotransmitter acetylcholine.

name: acid etching , dental
query: Query: acid etching , dental [SEP] Dental acid etching is preparation of tooth surfaces and dental materials with etching agents, usually phosphoric acid, to roughen the surface to increase adhesion or osteointegration.

name: acidosis , respiratory
query: Query: acidosis , respiratory [SEP] Respiratory acidosis is respiratory retention of carbon dioxide. It may be chronic or acute.

name: acoustic stimulation
query: Query: acoustic stimulation [SEP] Acoustic stimulation is use of sound to elicit a response in the nervous system.

name: acupuncture analgesia
query: Query: acupuncture analgesia [SEP] Acupuncture analgesia is analgesia produced by the insertion of acupuncture needles at certain acupuncture points on the body. This activates small myelinated nerve fibers in the muscle which transmit impulses to the spinal cord and then activate three centers - the spinal cord, midbrain and pituitary/hypothalamus - to produce analgesia.

name: acute coronary syndrome
query: Query: acute coronary syndrome [SEP] Acute coronary syndrome is an episode of myocardial ischemia that generally lasts longer than a transient anginal episode that ultimately may lead to myocardial infarction.

name: acute disease
query: Query: acute disease [SEP] Acute disease is disease having a short and relatively severe course.

name: adaptor protein complex 2
query: Query: adaptor protein complex 2 [SEP] Adaptor protein complex 2 is an adaptor protein complex primarily involved in the formation of clathrin-related endocytotic vesicles (endosomes) at the cell membrane.

name: adaptor protein complex delta subunits
query: Query: adaptor protein complex delta subunits [SEP] Adaptor protein complex delta subunits is a family of large adaptin protein subunits of approximately 130-kDa in size. They have been primarily found as components of adaptor protein complex 3.

name: adenocarcinoma in situ
query: Query: adenocarcinoma in situ [SEP] Adenocarcinoma in situ is a lesion with cytological characteristics associated with invasive adenocarcinoma but the tumor cells are confined to the glandular epithelial cells of origin. Adenocarcinoma in situ of the cervix and the lung are the most common.

name: adenoma , islet cell
query: Query: adenoma , islet cell [SEP] Islet cell adenoma is a benign tumor of the pancreatic islet cells. Usually it involves the INSULIN-producing pancreatic beta cells, as in insulinoma, resulting in hyperinsulinism.

name: adipocytes , white
query: Query: adipocytes , white [SEP] White adipocytes is fat cells with light coloration and few mitochondria. They contain a scant ring of cytoplasm surrounding a single large lipid droplet or vacuole.

name: adipose tissue , brown
query: Query: adipose tissue , brown [SEP] Brown adipose tissue is a thermogenic form of adipose tissue composed of brown adipocytes. It is found in newborns of many species including humans, and in hibernating mammals. Brown fat is richly vascularized, innervated, and densely packed with mitochondria which can generate heat directly from the stored lipids.

name: adiposity
query: Query: adiposity [SEP] Adiposity is the amount of fat or lipid deposit at a site or an organ in the body, an indicator of body fat status.

name: administration , buccal
query: Query: administration , buccal [SEP] Buccal administration is administration of a soluble dosage form between the cheek and gingiva. It may involve direct application of a drug onto the buccal mucosa, as by painting or spraying.

name: adolescent health
query: Query: adolescent health [SEP] Adolescent health is the concept covering the physical and mental conditions of adolescents.

name: adrenal rest tumor
query: Query: adrenal rest tumor [SEP] Adrenal rest tumor is neoplasm derived from displaced cells (rest cells) of the primordial adrenal glands, generally in patients with congenital adrenal hyperplasia. Adrenal rest tumors have been identified in testes; liver; and other tissues. They are dependent on adrenocorticotropin for growth and adrenal steroid secretion.

name: advance care planning
query: Query: advance care planning [SEP] Advance care planning is discussions with patients and/or their representatives about the goals and desired direction of the patient's care, particularly end-of-life care, in the event that the patient is or becomes incompetent to make decisions.

name: advertising
query: Query: advertising [SEP] Advertising is works about the act or practice of calling public attention to a product, service, need, etc., especially by paid announcements in newspapers, magazines, on radio, or on television. (Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed)

name: aerospace medicine
query: Query: aerospace medicine [SEP] Aerospace medicine is that branch of medicine dealing with the studies and effects of flight through the atmosphere or in space upon the human body and with the prevention or cure of physiological or psychological malfunctions arising from these effects. (from nasa Thesaurus)

name: agricultural irrigation
query: Query: agricultural irrigation [SEP] Agricultural irrigation is the routing of water to open or closed areas where it is used for agricultural purposes.

name: aid to families with dependent children
query: Query: aid to families with dependent children [SEP] Aid to families with dependent children is financial assistance provided by the government to indigent families with dependent children who meet certain requirements as defined by the Social Security Act, Title iv, in the u.s.

name: air filters
query: Query: air filters [SEP] Air filters is barriers used to separate and remove particulate matter from air.

name: air microbiology
query: Query: air microbiology [SEP] Air microbiology is the presence of bacteria, viruses, and fungi in the air. This term is not restricted to pathogenic organisms.

name: air pollution , indoor
query: Query: air pollution , indoor [SEP] Indoor air pollution is the contamination of indoor air.

name: alanine
query: Query: alanine [SEP] Alanine is a non-essential amino acid that occurs in high levels in its free state in plasma. It is produced from pyruvate by transamination. It is involved in sugar and acid metabolism, increases immunity, and provides energy for muscle tissue, brain, and the central nervous system.

name: alcohol withdrawal delirium
query: Query: alcohol withdrawal delirium [SEP] Alcohol withdrawal delirium is an acute organic mental disorder induced by cessation or reduction in chronic alcohol consumption. Clinical characteristics include confusion; delusions; vivid hallucinations; tremor; agitation; insomnia; and signs of autonomic hyperactivity (e.g., elevated blood pressure and heart rate, dilated pupils, and diaphoresis). This condition may occasionally be fatal. It was formerly called delirium tremens. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p1175)

name: alcohol withdrawal seizures
query: Query: alcohol withdrawal seizures [SEP] Alcohol withdrawal seizures is a condition where seizures occur in association with ethanol abuse (alcoholism) without other identifiable causes. Seizures usually occur within the first 6-48 hours after the cessation of alcohol intake, but may occur during periods of alcohol intoxication. Single generalized tonic-clonic motor seizures are the most common subtype, however, status epilepticus may occur. (Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p1174)

name: aldehyde dehydrogenase , mitochondrial
query: Query: aldehyde dehydrogenase , mitochondrial [SEP] Mitochondrial aldehyde dehydrogenase is an aldehyde dehydrogenase expressed in the mitochondrial matrix that is essential for the metabolism of ethanol.

name: algal proteins
query: Query: algal proteins [SEP] Algal proteins is proteins found in any species of algae.

name: allergy and immunology
query: Query: allergy and immunology [SEP] Allergy and immunology is a medical specialty concerned with the hypersensitivity of the individual to foreign substances and protection from the resultant infection or disorder.

name: allogeneic cells
query: Query: allogeneic cells [SEP] Allogeneic cells is cells from genetically different individuals of the same species to be used for cell- and tissue-based therapy; adoptive cell transfer; or adoptive immunotherapy.

name: alpha particles
query: Query: alpha particles [SEP] Alpha particles is positively charged particles composed of two protons and two neutrons, i.e. equivalent to helium nuclei, which are emitted during disintegration of heavy isotopes. Alpha rays have very strong ionizing power, but weak penetrability.

name: alternative splicing
query: Query: alternative splicing [SEP] Alternative splicing is a process whereby multiple rna transcripts are generated from a single gene. Alternative splicing involves the splicing together of other possible sets of exons during the processing of some, but not all, transcripts of the gene. Thus a particular exon may be connected to any one of several alternative exons to form a mature rna. The alternative forms of mature messenger rna produce protein isoforms in which one part of the isoforms is common while the other parts are different.

name: aluminum chloride
query: Query: aluminum chloride [SEP] Aluminum chloride is a compound with the chemical formula AlCl3; the anhydrous salt is used as a catalyst in organic chemical synthesis, and hydrated salts are used topically as antiperspirants, and for the management of hyperhydrosis.

name: ambulatory care information systems
query: Query: ambulatory care information systems [SEP] Ambulatory care information systems is information systems, usually computer-assisted, designed to store, manipulate, and retrieve information for planning, organizing, directing, and controlling administrative activities associated with the provision and utilization of ambulatory care services and facilities.

name: american civil war
query: Query: american civil war [SEP] American civil war is 1861-1865 conflict between the Union (Northern states) and the 11 Southern states that seceded and were organized as the Confederate States of America.

name: american dental association
query: Query: american dental association [SEP] American dental association is professional society representing the field of dentistry.

name: ammonia
query: Query: ammonia [SEP] Ammonia is a colorless alkaline gas. It is formed in the body during decomposition of organic materials during a large number of metabolically important reactions. Note that the aqueous form of ammonia is referred to as ammonium hydroxide.

name: amputation
query: Query: amputation [SEP] Amputation is the removal of a limb or other appendage or outgrowth of the body. (Dorland, 28th ed)

name: anal gland neoplasms
query: Query: anal gland neoplasms [SEP] Anal gland neoplasms is tumors or cancer of the anal gland.

name: anesthesia , dental
query: Query: anesthesia , dental [SEP] Dental anesthesia is a range of methods used to reduce pain and anxiety during dental procedures.

name: anger management therapy
query: Query: anger management therapy [SEP] Anger management therapy is system of psychological and/or therapeutic techniques used to control and or reduce the triggers, degrees, and effects of anger.

name: angiogenesis inhibitors
query: Query: angiogenesis inhibitors [SEP] Angiogenesis inhibitors is agents and endogenous substances that antagonize or inhibit the development of new blood vessels.

name: angioplasty , balloon , coronary
query: Query: angioplasty , balloon , coronary [SEP] Coronary balloon angioplasty is dilation of an occluded coronary artery (or arteries) by means of a balloon catheter to restore myocardial blood supply.

name: angiotensin ii type 1 receptor blockers
query: Query: angiotensin ii type 1 receptor blockers [SEP] Angiotensin ii type 1 receptor blockers is agents that antagonize angiotensin ii type 1 receptor. Included are angiotensin ii analogs such as saralasin and biphenylimidazoles such as losartan. Some are used as antihypertensive agents.

name: animal feed
query: Query: animal feed [SEP] Animal feed is foodstuff used especially for domestic and laboratory animals, or livestock.

name: animal migration
query: Query: animal migration [SEP] Animal migration is periodic movements of animals in response to seasonal changes or reproductive instinct. Hormonal changes are the trigger in at least some animals. Most migrations are made for reasons of climatic change, feeding, or breeding.

name: animal nutrition sciences
query: Query: animal nutrition sciences [SEP] Animal nutrition sciences is the study of nutrition processes, as well as the components of food, their actions, interaction, and balance in relation to health and disease in animals.

name: anonymous testing
query: Query: anonymous testing [SEP] Anonymous testing is testing in which the source of the specimen or the person being tested is not individually identified.

name: anterior capsule of the lens
query: Query: anterior capsule of the lens [SEP] Anterior capsule of the lens is the anterior aspect of the casing that surrounds the natural crystalline lens.

name: anterior thalamic nuclei
query: Query: anterior thalamic nuclei [SEP] Anterior thalamic nuclei is three nuclei located beneath the dorsal surface of the most rostral part of the thalamus. The group includes the anterodorsal nucleus, anteromedial nucleus, and anteroventral nucleus. All receive connections from the mamillary body and brain fornix, and project fibers to the cingulate body.

name: antibodies , bacterial
query: Query: antibodies , bacterial [SEP] Bacterial antibodies is immunoglobulins produced in a response to bacterial antigens.

name: antibody affinity
query: Query: antibody affinity [SEP] Antibody affinity is a measure of the binding strength between antibody and a simple hapten or antigen determinant. It depends on the closeness of stereochemical fit between antibody combining sites and antigen determinants, on the size of the area of contact between them, and on the distribution of charged and hydrophobic groups. It includes the concept of "avidity," which refers to the strength of the antigen-antibody bond after formation of reversible complexes.

name: antioxidant response elements
query: Query: antioxidant response elements [SEP] Antioxidant response elements is nucleotide sequences that are found in the promoter regions of the genes of stress-responsive and cytoprotective proteins, such as those encoding antioxidant and phase ii detoxification enzymes. nf-e2-related factor 2 containing transcription factors bind to these elements during induction of these genes.

name: aortic valve insufficiency
query: Query: aortic valve insufficiency [SEP] Aortic valve insufficiency is pathological condition characterized by the backflow of blood from the ascending aorta back into the left ventricle, leading to regurgitation. It is caused by diseases of the aortic valve or its surrounding tissue (aortic root).

name: aquatic organisms
query: Query: aquatic organisms [SEP] Aquatic organisms is organisms that live in water.

name: arginine
query: Query: arginine [SEP] Arginine is an essential amino acid that is physiologically active in the L-form.

name: arm
query: Query: arm [SEP] Arm is the superior part of the upper extremity between the shoulder and the elbow.

name: arthroplasty , replacement , finger
query: Query: arthroplasty , replacement , finger [SEP] Finger replacement arthroplasty is partial or total replacement of one or more fingers, or a finger joint.

name: artificial lens implant migration
query: Query: artificial lens implant migration [SEP] Artificial lens implant migration is the shifting and or tilting of implanted artificial lens resulting in impaired vision.

name: artificial limbs
query: Query: artificial limbs [SEP] Artificial limbs is prosthetic replacements for arms, legs, and parts thereof.

name: aspergillus niger
query: Query: aspergillus niger [SEP] Aspergillus niger is an imperfect fungus causing smut or black mold of several fruits and vegetables such as grapes, apricots, onions, and peanuts, and is a common contaminant of food.

name: athletes
query: Query: athletes [SEP] Athletes is individuals who have developed skills, physical stamina and strength or participants in sports or other physical activities.

name: atmosphere exposure chambers
query: Query: atmosphere exposure chambers [SEP] Atmosphere exposure chambers is experimental devices used in inhalation studies in which a person or animal is either partially or completely immersed in a chemically controlled atmosphere.

name: atp binding cassette transporter , subfamily g , member 1
query: Query: atp binding cassette transporter , subfamily g , member 1 [SEP] Member 1 subfamily g atp binding cassette transporter is atp binding cassette transporter that functions primarily as a lipid and cholesterol exporter in macrophages.  It may also function in intracellular lipid transport and homoeostasis.

name: atrial remodeling
query: Query: atrial remodeling [SEP] Atrial remodeling is long-term changes in the electrophysiological parameters and/or anatomical structures of the heart atria that result from prolonged changes in atrial rate, often associated with atrial fibrillation or long periods of intense exercise.

name: avian proteins
query: Query: avian proteins [SEP] Avian proteins is proteins obtained from species of birds.

name: axillary vein
query: Query: axillary vein [SEP] Axillary vein is the venous trunk of the upper limb; a continuation of the basilar and brachial veins running from the lower border of the teres major muscle to the outer border of the first rib where it becomes the subclavian vein.

name: bacillus subtilis
query: Query: bacillus subtilis [SEP] Bacillus subtilis is a species of gram-positive bacteria that is a common soil and water saprophyte.

name: bacteria , aerobic
query: Query: bacteria , aerobic [SEP] Aerobic bacteria is bacteria which require oxygen in order to grow and survive.

name: bacterial outer membrane
query: Query: bacterial outer membrane [SEP] Bacterial outer membrane is the outermost cell envelope of gram-negative bacteria composed of phospholipids; lipopolysaccharides (lps), and bacterial outer membrane proteins. The bacterial outer membrane lps demonstrates cytotoxicity (see lipid a and bacterial o antigen).

name: bacterial translocation
query: Query: bacterial translocation [SEP] Bacterial translocation is the passage of viable bacteria from the gastrointestinal tract to extra-intestinal sites, such as the mesenteric lymph node complex, liver, spleen, kidney, and blood. Factors that promote bacterial translocation include overgrowth with gram-negative enteric bacilli, impaired host immune defenses, and injury to the intestinal mucosa resulting in increased intestinal permeability. Bacterial translocation from the lung to the circulation is also possible and sometimes accompanies mechanical ventilation.

name: balloon occlusion
query: Query: balloon occlusion [SEP] Balloon occlusion is use of a balloon catheter to block the flow of blood through an artery or vein.

name: baltimore
query: Query: baltimore [SEP] Baltimore is a city located in Maryland.

name: base pair mismatch
query: Query: base pair mismatch [SEP] Base pair mismatch is the presence of an uncomplimentary base in double-stranded dna caused by spontaneous deamination of cytosine or adenine, mismatching during homologous recombination, or errors in dna replication. Multiple, sequential base pair mismatches lead to formation of heteroduplex dna; (nucleic acid heteroduplexes).

name: basic reproduction number
query: Query: basic reproduction number [SEP] Basic reproduction number is the expected number of new cases of an infection caused by an infected individual, amongst susceptible contacts only.

name: bayes theorem
query: Query: bayes theorem [SEP] Bayes theorem is a theorem in probability theory named for Thomas Bayes (1702-1761). In epidemiology, it is used to obtain the probability of disease in a group of people with some characteristic on the basis of the overall rate of that disease and of the likelihood of that characteristic in healthy and diseased individuals. The most familiar application is in clinical decision analysis where it is used for estimating the probability of a particular diagnosis given the appearance of some symptoms or test result.

name: bcg vaccine
query: Query: bcg vaccine [SEP] Bcg vaccine is an active immunizing agent and a viable avirulent attenuated strain of mycobacterium bovis, which confers immunity to mycobacterial infections. It is used also in immunotherapy of neoplasms due to its stimulation of antibodies and non-specific immunity.

name: benzyl alcohol
query: Query: benzyl alcohol [SEP] Benzyl alcohol is a colorless liquid with a sharp burning taste and slight odor. It is used as a local anesthetic and to reduce pain associated with lidocaine injection. Also, it is used in the manufacture of other benzyl compounds, as a pharmaceutic aid, and in perfumery and flavoring.

name: biliary fistula
query: Query: biliary fistula [SEP] Biliary fistula is abnormal passage in any organ of the biliary tract or between biliary organs and other organs.

name: biomarkers , pharmacological
query: Query: biomarkers , pharmacological [SEP] Pharmacological biomarkers is measurable biological parameters that serve for drug development, safety and dosing (drug monitoring).

name: biomedical engineering
query: Query: biomedical engineering [SEP] Biomedical engineering is application of principles and practices of engineering science to biomedical research and health care.

name: bipolar disorder
query: Query: bipolar disorder [SEP] Bipolar disorder is a major affective disorder marked by severe mood swings (manic or major depressive episodes) and a tendency to remission and recurrence.

name: bite force
query: Query: bite force [SEP] Bite force is the force applied by the masticatory muscles in dental occlusion.

name: blast crisis
query: Query: blast crisis [SEP] Blast crisis is an advanced phase of chronic myelogenous leukemia, characterized by a rapid increase in the proportion of immature white blood cells (blasts) in the blood and bone marrow to greater than 30%.

name: blindness , cortical
query: Query: blindness , cortical [SEP] Cortical blindness is total loss of vision in all or part of the visual field due to bilateral occipital lobe (i.e., visual cortex) damage or dysfunction. Anton syndrome is characterized by the psychic denial of true, organic cortical blindness. (Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p460)

name: blood circulation time
query: Query: blood circulation time [SEP] Blood circulation time is determination of the shortest time interval between the injection of a substance in the vein and its arrival at some distant site in sufficient concentration to produce a recognizable end result. It represents approximately the inverse of the average velocity of blood flow between two points.

name: blood gas analysis
query: Query: blood gas analysis [SEP] Blood gas analysis is measurement of oxygen and carbon dioxide in the blood.

name: blood loss , surgical
query: Query: blood loss , surgical [SEP] Surgical blood loss is loss of blood during a surgical procedure.

name: blotting , western
query: Query: blotting , western [SEP] Western blotting is identification of proteins or peptides that have been electrophoretically separated by blot transferring from the electrophoresis gel to strips of nitrocellulose paper, followed by labeling with antibody probes.

name: blue toe syndrome
query: Query: blue toe syndrome [SEP] Blue toe syndrome is a condition that is caused by recurring atheroembolism in the lower extremities. It is characterized by cyanotic discoloration of the toes, usually the first, fourth, and fifth toes. Discoloration may extend to the lateral aspect of the foot. Despite the gangrene-like appearance, blue toes may respond to conservative therapy without amputation.

name: body image
query: Query: body image [SEP] Body image is individuals' concept of their own bodies.

name: body packing
query: Query: body packing [SEP] Body packing is concealing of drugs within the gastrointestinal tract or other body orifice for purposes of drug smuggling or to avoid detection by law enforcement. Contraband other than drugs is also sometimes smuggled this way.

name: bone density
query: Query: bone density [SEP] Bone density is the amount of mineral per square centimeter of bone. This is the definition used in clinical practice. Actual bone density would be expressed in grams per milliliter. It is most frequently measured by x-ray absorptiometry or tomography, x ray computed. Bone density is an important predictor for osteoporosis.

name: bone marrow examination
query: Query: bone marrow examination [SEP] Bone marrow examination is removal of bone marrow and evaluation of its histologic picture.

name: book reviews as topic
query: Query: book reviews as topic [SEP] Book reviews as topic is works about critical analyses of books or other monographic works.

name: border disease
query: Query: border disease [SEP] Border disease is congenital disorder of lambs caused by a virus closely related to or identical with certain strains of bovine viral diarrhea virus.

name: brain mapping
query: Query: brain mapping [SEP] Brain mapping is imaging techniques used to colocalize sites of brain functions or physiological activity with brain structures.

name: breast density
query: Query: breast density [SEP] Breast density is measurement of relative composition of different breast tissue types often determined from mammography; ultrasonography; or mri.

name: breast milk expression
query: Query: breast milk expression [SEP] Breast milk expression is the act of evacuating breast milk by hand or with a pump.

name: breast neoplasms , male
query: Query: breast neoplasms , male [SEP] Male breast neoplasms is any neoplasms of the male breast. These occur infrequently in males in developed countries, the incidence being about 1% of that in females.

name: british columbia
query: Query: british columbia [SEP] British columbia is a province of Canada on the Pacific coast. Its capital is Victoria. The name given in 1858 derives from the Columbia River which was named by the American captain Robert Gray for his ship Columbia which in turn was named for Columbus. (From Webster's New Geographical Dictionary, 1988, p178 & Room, Brewer's Dictionary of Names, 1992, p81-2)

name: bronchial arteries
query: Query: bronchial arteries [SEP] Bronchial arteries is left bronchial arteries arise from the thoracic aorta, the right from the first aortic intercostal or the upper left bronchial artery; they supply the bronchi and the lower trachea.

name: buffers
query: Query: buffers [SEP] Buffers is a chemical system that functions to control the levels of specific ions in solution. When the level of hydrogen ion in solution is controlled the system is called a pH buffer.

name: burning mouth syndrome
query: Query: burning mouth syndrome [SEP] Burning mouth syndrome is a group of painful oral symptoms associated with a burning or similar sensation. There is usually a significant organic component with a degree of functional overlay; it is not limited to the psychophysiologic group of disorders.

name: cadmium poisoning
query: Query: cadmium poisoning [SEP] Cadmium poisoning is poisoning occurring after exposure to cadmium compounds or fumes. It may cause gastrointestinal syndromes, anemia, or pneumonitis.

name: calcium channel agonists
query: Query: calcium channel agonists [SEP] Calcium channel agonists is agents that increase calcium influx into calcium channels of excitable tissues. This causes vasoconstriction in vascular smooth muscle and/or cardiac muscle cells as well as stimulation of insulin release from pancreatic islets. Therefore, tissue-selective calcium agonists have the potential to combat cardiac failure and endocrinological disorders. They have been used primarily in experimental studies in cell and tissue culture.

name: cancer survivors
query: Query: cancer survivors [SEP] Cancer survivors is persons who have experienced prolonged survival with or following malignant neoplastic disease.

name: cancer vaccines
query: Query: cancer vaccines [SEP] Cancer vaccines is vaccines or candidate vaccines designed to prevent or treat cancer. Vaccines are produced using the patient's own whole tumor cells as the source of antigens, or using tumor-specific antigens, often recombinantly produced.

name: candida albicans
query: Query: candida albicans [SEP] Candida albicans is a unicellular budding fungus which is the principal pathogenic species causing candidiasis (moniliasis).

name: carbon fiber
query: Query: carbon fiber [SEP] Carbon fiber is fiber with a diameter of approximately 5 to 10 micrometers that is composed mostly of carbon atoms. It has a variety of applications.

name: carbon isotopes
query: Query: carbon isotopes [SEP] Carbon isotopes is stable carbon atoms that have the same atomic number as the element carbon, but differ in atomic weight. c-13 is a stable carbon isotope.

name: carcinoma , giant cell
query: Query: carcinoma , giant cell [SEP] Giant cell carcinoma is an epithelial neoplasm characterized by unusually large anaplastic cells. It is highly malignant with fulminant clinical course, bizarre histologic appearance and poor prognosis. It is most common in the lung and thyroid. (From Stedman, 25th ed & Segen, Dictionary of Modern Medicine, 1992)

name: carcinoma , lewis lung
query: Query: carcinoma , lewis lung [SEP] Lewis lung carcinoma is a carcinoma discovered by Dr. Margaret r. Lewis of the Wistar Institute in 1951. This tumor originated spontaneously as a carcinoma of the lung of a c57bl mouse. The tumor does not appear to be grossly hemorrhagic and the majority of the tumor tissue is a semifirm homogeneous mass. (From Cancer Chemother Rep 2 1972 Nov;(3)1:325) It is also called 3ll and llc and is used as a transplantable malignancy.

name: carcinoma , renal cell
query: Query: carcinoma , renal cell [SEP] Renal cell carcinoma is a heterogeneous group of sporadic or hereditary carcinoma derived from cells of the kidneys. There are several subtypes including the clear cells, the papillary, the chromophobe, the collecting duct, the spindle cells (sarcomatoid), or mixed cell-type carcinoma.

name: cardio ankle vascular index
query: Query: cardio ankle vascular index [SEP] Cardio ankle vascular index is an index of arterial stiffness obtained from pulse wave velocity measurements between the heart and the ankle.

name: carotid artery thrombosis
query: Query: carotid artery thrombosis [SEP] Carotid artery thrombosis is blood clot formation in any part of the carotid arteries. This may produce carotid stenosis or occlusion of the vessel, leading to transient ischemic attack; cerebral infarction; or amaurosis fugax.

name: casein kinase i
query: Query: casein kinase i [SEP] Casein kinase i is a casein kinase that was originally described as a monomeric enzyme with a molecular weight of 30-40 kDa. Several isoenzymes of casein kinase i have been found which are encoded by separate genes. Many of the casein kinase i isoenzymes have been shown to play distinctive roles in intracellular signal transduction.

name: catalytic domain
query: Query: catalytic domain [SEP] Catalytic domain is the region of an enzyme that interacts with its substrate to cause the enzymatic reaction.

name: cataract
query: Query: cataract [SEP] Cataract is partial or complete opacity on or in the lens or capsule of one or both eyes, impairing vision or causing blindness. The many kinds of cataract are classified by their morphology (size, shape, location) or etiology (cause and time of occurrence). (Dorland, 27th ed)

name: cathepsin a
query: Query: cathepsin a [SEP] Cathepsin a is a carboxypeptidase that catalyzes the release of a C-terminal amino acid with a broad specificity. It also plays a role in the lysosomes by protecting beta-galactosidase and neuraminidase from degradation. It was formerly classified as ec 3.4.12.1 and ec 3.4.21.13.

name: cathepsin c
query: Query: cathepsin c [SEP] Cathepsin c is a papain-like cysteine protease that has specificity for amino terminal dipeptides. The enzyme plays a role in the activation of several pro-inflammatory serine proteases by removal of their aminoterminal inhibitory dipeptides. Genetic mutations that cause loss of cathepsin c activity in humans are associated with papillon-lefevre disease.

name: catheterization , peripheral
query: Query: catheterization , peripheral [SEP] Peripheral catheterization is insertion of a catheter into a peripheral artery, vein, or airway for diagnostic or therapeutic purposes.

name: cause of death
query: Query: cause of death [SEP] Cause of death is factors which produce cessation of all vital bodily functions. They can be analyzed from an epidemiologic viewpoint.

name: cellular apoptosis susceptibility protein
query: Query: cellular apoptosis susceptibility protein [SEP] Cellular apoptosis susceptibility protein is a nucleocytoplasmic transport protein that binds to alpha karyopherins and ran gtp binding protein inside the cell nucleus and participates in their export into cytoplasm. It is also associated with the regulation of apoptosis and microtubule assembly.

name: cell wall skeleton
query: Query: cell wall skeleton [SEP] Cell wall skeleton is a mucoprotein found in the cell wall of various types of bacteria. It has adjuvant and antitumor activities and has been used to augment the production of lymphokine-activated killer (lak) cells.

name: central african republic
query: Query: central african republic [SEP] Central african republic is a republic in central Africa south of chad and sudan, north of democratic republic of the congo, and east of cameroon. The capital is Bangui.

name: central supply , hospital
query: Query: central supply , hospital [SEP] Hospital central supply is hospital department responsible for receiving, storing, and distributing medical and surgical supplies and equipment.

name: central venous pressure
query: Query: central venous pressure [SEP] Central venous pressure is the blood pressure in the central large veins of the body. It is distinguished from peripheral venous pressure which occurs in an extremity.

name: cerebrovascular circulation
query: Query: cerebrovascular circulation [SEP] Cerebrovascular circulation is the circulation of blood through the blood vessels of the brain.

name: cervical cord
query: Query: cervical cord [SEP] Cervical cord is the segment of the spinal cord within the cervical vertebrae.

name: cervix mucus
query: Query: cervix mucus [SEP] Cervix mucus is a slightly alkaline secretion of the endocervical glands. The consistency and amount are dependent on the physiological hormone changes in the menstrual cycle. It contains the glycoprotein mucin, amino acids, sugar, enzymes, and electrolytes, with a water content up to 90%. The mucus is a useful protection against the ascent of bacteria and sperm into the uterus. (From Dictionary of Obstetrics and Gynecology, 1988)

name: character
query: Query: character [SEP] Character is in current usage, approximately equivalent to personality. The sum of the relatively fixed personality traits and habitual modes of response of an individual.

name: checklist
query: Query: checklist [SEP] Checklist is aid for consistent recording of data such as tasks completed and observations noted.

name: chemistry , analytic

query: Query: egypt [SEP] Egypt is a country in northern Africa, bordering the Mediterranean Sea, between Libya and the Gaza Strip, and the Red Sea north of Sudan, and includes the Asian Sinai Peninsula Its capital is Cairo.

name: elasticity imaging techniques
query: Query: elasticity imaging techniques [SEP] Elasticity imaging techniques is non-invasive imaging methods based on the mechanical response of an object to a vibrational or impulsive force. It is used for determining the viscoelastic properties of tissue, and thereby differentiating soft from hard inclusions in tissue such as microcalcifications, and some cancer lesions. Most techniques use ultrasound to create the images - eliciting the response with an ultrasonic radiation force and/or recording displacements of the tissue by Doppler ultrasonography.

name: elastic modulus
query: Query: elastic modulus [SEP] Elastic modulus is numerical expression indicating the measure of stiffness in a material. It is defined by the ratio of stress in a unit area of substance to the resulting deformation (strain). This allows the behavior of a material under load (such as bone) to be calculated.

name: elective surgical procedures
query: Query: elective surgical procedures [SEP] Elective surgical procedures is surgery which could be postponed or not done at all without danger to the patient. Elective surgery includes procedures to correct non-life-threatening medical problems as well as to alleviate conditions causing psychological stress or other potential risk to patients, e.g., cosmetic or contraceptive surgery.

name: electric fish
query: Query: electric fish [SEP] Electric fish is fishes which generate an electric discharge. The voltage of the discharge varies from weak to strong in various groups of fish. The electric organ and electroplax are of prime interest in this group. They occur in more than one family.

name: electric organ
query: Query: electric organ [SEP] Electric organ is in about 250 species of electric fishes, modified muscle fibers forming disklike multinucleate plates arranged in stacks like batteries in series and embedded in a gelatinous matrix. a large torpedo ray may have half a million plates. Muscles in different parts of the body may be modified, i.e., the trunk and tail in the electric eel, the hyobranchial apparatus in the electric ray, and extrinsic eye muscles in the stargazers. Powerful electric organs emit pulses in brief bursts several times a second. They serve to stun prey and ward off predators. a large torpedo ray can produce of shock of more than 200 volts, capable of stunning a human. (Storer et al., General Zoology, 6th ed, p672)

name: electronic mail
query: Query: electronic mail [SEP] Electronic mail is messages between computer users via computer communication networks. This feature duplicates most of the features of paper mail, such as forwarding, multiple copies, and attachments of images and other file types, but with a speed advantage. The term also refers to an individual message sent in this way.

name: electronic prescribing
query: Query: electronic prescribing [SEP] Electronic prescribing is the use of computer communication networks to store and transmit medical prescriptions.

name: electronics , medical
query: Query: electronics , medical [SEP] Medical electronics is the research and development of electrical equipment and supplies for such medical applications as diagnosis, therapy, research, anesthesia control, cardiac control, and surgery. (From McGraw-Hill Dictionary of Scientific and Technical Terms, 6th ed)

name: electrons
query: Query: electrons [SEP] Electrons is stable elementary particles having the smallest known negative charge, present in all elements; also called negatrons. Positively charged electrons are called positrons. The numbers, energies and arrangement of electrons around atomic nuclei determine the chemical identities of elements. Beams of electrons are called cathode rays.

name: electron spin resonance spectroscopy
query: Query: electron spin resonance spectroscopy [SEP] Electron spin resonance spectroscopy is a technique applicable to the wide variety of substances which exhibit paramagnetism because of the magnetic moments of unpaired electrons. The spectra are useful for detection and identification, for determination of electron structure, for study of interactions between molecules, and for measurement of nuclear spins and moments. (From McGraw-Hill Encyclopedia of Science and Technology, 7th edition) Electron nuclear double resonance (endor) spectroscopy is a variant of the technique which can give enhanced resolution. Electron spin resonance analysis can now be used in vivo, including imaging applications such as magnetic resonance imaging.

name: electron transport complex iv
query: Query: electron transport complex iv [SEP] Electron transport complex iv is a multisubunit enzyme complex containing cytochrome a group; cytochrome a3; two copper atoms; and 13 different protein subunits. It is the terminal oxidase complex of the respiratory chain and collects electrons that are transferred from the reduced cytochrome c group and donates them to molecular oxygen, which is then reduced to water. The redox reaction is simultaneously coupled to the transport of protons across the inner mitochondrial membrane.

name: electrophoresis , agar gel
query: Query: electrophoresis , agar gel [SEP] Agar gel electrophoresis is electrophoresis in which agar or agarose gel is used as the diffusion medium.

name: electrophoretic mobility shift assay
query: Query: electrophoretic mobility shift assay [SEP] Electrophoretic mobility shift assay is an electrophoretic technique for assaying the binding of one compound to another. Typically one compound is labeled to follow its mobility during electrophoresis. If the labeled compound is bound by the other compound, then the mobility of the labeled compound through the electrophoretic medium will be retarded.

name: elementary particle interactions
query: Query: elementary particle interactions [SEP] Elementary particle interactions is the interactions of particles responsible for their scattering and transformations (decays and reactions). Because of interactions, an isolated particle may decay into other particles. Two particles passing near each other may transform, perhaps into the same particles but with changed momenta (elastic scattering) or into other particles (inelastic scattering). Interactions fall into three groups: strong, electromagnetic, and weak. (From McGraw-Hill Encyclopedia of Science & Technology, 7th ed)

name: elimination disorders
query: Query: elimination disorders [SEP] Elimination disorders is excretory-related psychiatric disorders usually diagnosed in infancy or childhood.

name: embryo disposition
query: Query: embryo disposition [SEP] Embryo disposition is utilization or disposal of an embryo that is fertilized but not immediately transplanted and resulting course of action.

name: emergence delirium
query: Query: emergence delirium [SEP] Emergence delirium is a form of delirium which occurs after general anesthesia.

name: emergency medical tags
query: Query: emergency medical tags [SEP] Emergency medical tags is a bracelet or necklace worn by an individual that alerts emergency personnel of medical information for that individual which could affect their condition or treatment.

name: empathy
query: Query: empathy [SEP] Empathy is an individual's objective and insightful awareness of the feelings and behavior of another person. It should be distinguished from sympathy, which is usually nonobjective and noncritical. It includes caring, which is the demonstration of an awareness of and a concern for the good of others. (From Bioethics Thesaurus, 1992)

name: employee discipline
query: Query: employee discipline [SEP] Employee discipline is regulations or conditions imposed on employees by management in order to correct or prevent behaviors which are counterproductive to the organization.

name: endemic diseases
query: Query: endemic diseases [SEP] Endemic diseases is the constant presence of diseases or infectious agents within a given geographic area or population group. It may also refer to the usual prevalence of a given disease with such area or group. It includes holoendemic and hyperendemic diseases. a holoendemic disease is one for which a high prevalent level of infection begins early in life and affects most of the child population, leading to a state of equilibrium such that the adult population shows evidence of the disease much less commonly than do children (malaria in many communities is a holoendemic disease). a hyperendemic disease is one that is constantly present at a high incidence and/or prevalence rate and affects all groups equally. (Last, a Dictionary of Epidemiology, 3d ed, p53, 78, 80)

name: endocrine surgical procedures
query: Query: endocrine surgical procedures [SEP] Endocrine surgical procedures is surgery performed on any endocrine gland.

name: endothelial progenitor cells
query: Query: endothelial progenitor cells [SEP] Endothelial progenitor cells is cells derived from bone marrow that circulate in the adult bloodstream and possess the potential to proliferate and differentiate into mature endothelial cells.

name: endothelium , corneal
query: Query: endothelium , corneal [SEP] Corneal endothelium is single layer of large flattened cells covering the surface of the cornea.

name: enzyme replacement therapy
query: Query: enzyme replacement therapy [SEP] Enzyme replacement therapy is therapeutic replacement or supplementation of defective or missing enzymes to alleviate the effects of enzyme deficiency (e.g., glucosylceramidase replacement for gaucher disease).

name: enzyme stability
query: Query: enzyme stability [SEP] Enzyme stability is the extent to which an enzyme retains its structural conformation or its activity when subjected to storage, isolation, and purification or various other physical or chemical manipulations, including proteolytic enzymes and heat.

name: epidermal cyst
query: Query: epidermal cyst [SEP] Epidermal cyst is intradermal or subcutaneous saclike structure, the wall of which is stratified epithelium containing keratohyalin granules.

name: epidural space
query: Query: epidural space [SEP] Epidural space is space between the dura mater and the walls of the vertebral canal.

name: epilepsy , temporal lobe
query: Query: epilepsy , temporal lobe [SEP] Temporal lobe epilepsy is a localization-related (focal) form of epilepsy characterized by recurrent seizures that arise from foci within the temporal lobe, most commonly from its mesial aspect. a wide variety of psychic phenomena may be associated, including illusions, hallucinations, dyscognitive states, and affective experiences. The majority of complex partial seizures (see epilepsy, complex partial) originate from the temporal lobes. Temporal lobe seizures may be classified by etiology as cryptogenic, familial, or symptomatic. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p321).

name: epithelial sodium channel agonists
query: Query: epithelial sodium channel agonists [SEP] Epithelial sodium channel agonists is compounds that either stimulate the opening or prevent closure of epithelial sodium ion channels.

name: epithelial sodium channels
query: Query: epithelial sodium channels [SEP] Epithelial sodium channels is sodium channels found on salt-reabsorbing epithelial cells that line the distal nephron; the distal colon; salivary ducts; sweat glands; and the lung. They are AMILORIDE-sensitive and play a critical role in the control of sodium balance, blood volume, and blood pressure.

name: epitope mapping
query: Query: epitope mapping [SEP] Epitope mapping is methods used for studying the interactions of antibodies with specific regions of protein antigens. Important applications of epitope mapping are found within the area of immunochemistry.

name: equipment contamination
query: Query: equipment contamination [SEP] Equipment contamination is the presence of an infectious agent on instruments, prostheses, or other inanimate articles.

name: equipment failure analysis
query: Query: equipment failure analysis [SEP] Equipment failure analysis is the evaluation of incidents involving the loss of function of a device. These evaluations are used for a variety of purposes such as to determine the failure rates, the causes of failures, costs of failures, and the reliability and maintainability of devices.

name: erythrocyte transfusion
query: Query: erythrocyte transfusion [SEP] Erythrocyte transfusion is the transfer of erythrocytes from a donor to a recipient or reinfusion to the donor.

name: essential hypertension
query: Query: essential hypertension [SEP] Essential hypertension is hypertension that occurs without known cause, or preexisting renal disease. Associated polymorphisms for a number of genes have been identified, including agt, gnb3, and ece1. omim: 145500

name: estrogen receptor alpha
query: Query: estrogen receptor alpha [SEP] Estrogen receptor alpha is one of the estrogen receptors that has marked affinity for estradiol. Its expression and function differs from, and in some ways opposes, estrogen receptor beta.

name: european continental ancestry group
query: Query: european continental ancestry group [SEP] European continental ancestry group is individuals whose ancestral origins are in the continent of Europe.

name: excitatory amino acids
query: Query: excitatory amino acids [SEP] Excitatory amino acids is endogenous amino acids released by neurons as excitatory neurotransmitters. Glutamic acid is the most common excitatory neurotransmitter in the brain. Aspartic acid has been regarded as an excitatory transmitter for many years, but the extent of its role as a transmitter is unclear.

name: excitatory amino acid transporter 2
query: Query: excitatory amino acid transporter 2 [SEP] Excitatory amino acid transporter 2 is a glutamate plasma membrane transporter protein found in astrocytes and in the liver.

name: excitatory amino acid transporter 5
query: Query: excitatory amino acid transporter 5 [SEP] Excitatory amino acid transporter 5 is a glutamate plasma membrane transporter protein that is primarily expressed in the retina.

name: expert systems
query: Query: expert systems [SEP] Expert systems is computer programs based on knowledge developed from consultation with experts on a problem, and the processing and/or formalizing of this knowledge using these programs in such a manner that the problems may be solved.

name: expressed sequence tags
query: Query: expressed sequence tags [SEP] Expressed sequence tags is partial cDNA (dna, complementary) sequences that are unique to the cDNAs from which they were derived.

name: extinction , biological
query: Query: extinction , biological [SEP] Biological extinction is the ceasing of existence of a species or taxonomic groups of organisms.

name: extreme cold weather
query: Query: extreme cold weather [SEP] Extreme cold weather is below normal weather temperatures that may lead to serious health problems. Extreme cold is a dangerous situation that can bring on health emergencies in susceptible people.

name: eye color
query: Query: eye color [SEP] Eye color is color of the iris.

name: eye infections , viral
query: Query: eye infections , viral [SEP] Viral eye infections is infections of the eye caused by minute intracellular agents. These infections may lead to severe inflammation in various parts of the eye - conjunctiva, iris, eyelids, etc. Several viruses have been identified as the causative agents. Among these are Herpesvirus, Adenovirus, Poxvirus, and Myxovirus.

name: facial asymmetry
query: Query: facial asymmetry [SEP] Facial asymmetry is congenital or acquired asymmetry of the face.

name: facility regulation and control
query: Query: facility regulation and control [SEP] Facility regulation and control is formal voluntary or governmental procedures and standards required of hospitals and health or other facilities to improve operating efficiency, and for the protection of the consumer.

name: factor for inversion stimulation protein
query: Query: factor for inversion stimulation protein [SEP] Factor for inversion stimulation protein is a highly abundant dna binding protein whose expression is strongly correlated with the growth phase of bacteria. The protein plays a role in regulating dna topology and activation of ribosomal rna transcription. It was originally identified as a factor required for inversion stimulation by the Hin recombinase of salmonella and Gin site-specific recombinase of bacteriophage mu.

name: factor va
query: Query: factor va [SEP] Factor va is activated form of factor v. It is an essential cofactor for the activation of prothrombin catalyzed by factor Xa.

name: factor vii
query: Query: factor vii [SEP] Factor vii is heat- and storage-stable plasma protein that is activated by tissue thromboplastin to form factor VIIa in the extrinsic pathway of blood coagulation. The activated form then catalyzes the activation of factor x to factor Xa.

name: factor xi deficiency
query: Query: factor xi deficiency [SEP] Factor xi deficiency is a hereditary deficiency of blood coagulation factor xi (also known as plasma thromboplastin antecedent or pta or antihemophilic factor c) resulting in a systemic blood-clotting defect called hemophilia c or Rosenthal's syndrome, that may resemble classical hemophilia.

name: faculty , medical
query: Query: faculty , medical [SEP] Medical faculty is teaching and administrative staff having academic rank in a medical school.

name: fast foods
query: Query: fast foods [SEP] Fast foods is prepared food that is ready to eat or partially prepared food that has a final preparation time of a few minutes or less.

name: fatal outcome
query: Query: fatal outcome [SEP] Fatal outcome is death resulting from the presence of a disease in an individual, as shown by a single case report or a limited number of patients. This should be differentiated from death, the physiological cessation of life and from mortality, an epidemiological or statistical concept.

name: fathers
query: Query: fathers [SEP] Fathers is male parents, human or animal.

name: fatty acid transport proteins
query: Query: fatty acid transport proteins [SEP] Fatty acid transport proteins is a broad category of membrane transport proteins that specifically transport free fatty acids across cellular membranes. They play an important role in lipid metabolism in cells that utilize free fatty acids as an energy source.

name: fatty liver , alcoholic
query: Query: fatty liver , alcoholic [SEP] Alcoholic fatty liver is lipid infiltration of the hepatic parenchymal cells that is due to alcohol abuse. The fatty changes in the alcoholic fatty liver may be reversible, depending on the amounts of triglycerides accumulated.

name: feasibility studies
query: Query: feasibility studies [SEP] Feasibility studies is studies to determine the advantages or disadvantages, practicability, or capability of accomplishing a projected plan, study, or project.

name: febrile neutropenia
query: Query: febrile neutropenia [SEP] Febrile neutropenia is fever accompanied by a significant reduction in the number of neutrophils.

name: fecal incontinence
query: Query: fecal incontinence [SEP] Fecal incontinence is failure of voluntary control of the anal sphincters, with involuntary passage of feces and flatus.

name: feedback
query: Query: feedback [SEP] Feedback is a mechanism of communication within a system in that the input signal generates an output response which returns to influence the continued activity or productivity of that system.

name: fees , medical
query: Query: fees , medical [SEP] Medical fees is amounts charged to the patient as payer for medical services.

name: femoral artery
query: Query: femoral artery [SEP] Femoral artery is the main artery of the thigh, a continuation of the external iliac artery.

name: femoral neoplasms
query: Query: femoral neoplasms [SEP] Femoral neoplasms is new abnormal growth of tissue in the femur.

name: ferric compounds
query: Query: ferric compounds [SEP] Ferric compounds is inorganic or organic compounds containing trivalent iron.

name: fertility clinics
query: Query: fertility clinics [SEP] Fertility clinics is health clinics offering fertility treatment services.

name: fetal blood
query: Query: fetal blood [SEP] Fetal blood is blood of the fetus. Exchange of nutrients and waste between the fetal and maternal blood occurs via the placenta. The cord blood is blood contained in the umbilical vessels (umbilical cord) at the time of delivery.

name: fetal nutrition disorders
query: Query: fetal nutrition disorders [SEP] Fetal nutrition disorders is disorders caused by nutritional imbalance, either overnutrition or undernutrition, in the fetus in utero.

name: fetal research
query: Query: fetal research [SEP] Fetal research is experimentation on, or using the organs or tissues from, a human or other mammalian conceptus in the postembryonic period, after the major structures have been outlined. In humans, this corresponds to the period from the third month after fertilization until birth.

name: fetal resorption
query: Query: fetal resorption [SEP] Fetal resorption is the disintegration and assimilation of the dead fetus in the uterus at any stage after the completion of organogenesis which, in humans, is after the 9th week of gestation. It does not include embryo resorption (see embryo loss).

name: fetal stem cells
query: Query: fetal stem cells [SEP] Fetal stem cells is cells derived from a fetus that retain the ability to divide, proliferate and provide progenitor cells that can differentiate into specialized cells.

name: fibroblast growth factor 10
query: Query: fibroblast growth factor 10 [SEP] Fibroblast growth factor 10 is a fibroblast growth factor that is a mitogen for keratinocytes. It activates fibroblast growth factor receptor 2b and is involved in lung and limb development.

name: fibronectin type iii domain
query: Query: fibronectin type iii domain [SEP] Fibronectin type iii domain is a highly conserved immunoglobulin-like protein domain of about 100 amino acids that forms a beta sandwich structure.

name: financial management , hospital
query: Query: financial management , hospital [SEP] Hospital financial management is the obtaining and management of funds for hospital needs and responsibility for fiscal affairs.

name: financial statements
query: Query: financial statements [SEP] Financial statements is formal and structured record of financial activities of a business, person, or other entity.

name: financing , construction
query: Query: financing , construction [SEP] Construction financing is funding resources and procedures for capital improvement or the construction of facilities.

name: first aid
query: Query: first aid [SEP] First aid is emergency care or treatment given to a person who suddenly becomes ill or injured before full medical services become available.

name: fiscal policy
query: Query: fiscal policy [SEP] Fiscal policy is use of government spending and taxation to influence the economy.

name: fixation , ocular
query: Query: fixation , ocular [SEP] Ocular fixation is positioning and accommodation of eyes that allows the image to be brought into place on the fovea centralis of each eye.

name: flank pain
query: Query: flank pain [SEP] Flank pain is pain emanating from below the ribs and above the ilium.

name: fluoride poisoning
query: Query: fluoride poisoning [SEP] Fluoride poisoning is poisoning that results from chronic or acute ingestion, injection, inhalation, or skin absorption of fluoride compounds.

name: focal epithelial hyperplasia
query: Query: focal epithelial hyperplasia [SEP] Focal epithelial hyperplasia is hyperplasia of the mucous membrane of the lips, tongue, and less commonly, the buccal mucosa, floor of the mouth, and palate, presenting soft, painless, round to oval sessile papules about 1 to 4 mm in diameter. The condition usually occurs in children and young adults and has familial predilection, lasting for several months, sometimes years, before running its course. a viral etiology is suspected, the isolated organism being usually the human papillomavirus. (Jablonski, Illustrated Dictionary of Dentistry; Belshe, Textbook of Human Virology, 2d ed, p954)

name: focal infection , dental
query: Query: focal infection , dental [SEP] Dental focal infection is secondary or systemic infections due to dissemination throughout the body of microorganisms whose primary focus of infection lies in the periodontal tissues.

name: food , organic
query: Query: food , organic [SEP] Organic food is food that is grown or manufactured in accordance with nationally regulated production standards that include restrictions on the use of pesticides, non-organic fertilizers, genetic engineering, growth hormones, irradiation, antibiotics, and non-organic ingredients.

name: food deprivation
query: Query: food deprivation [SEP] Food deprivation is the withholding of food in a structured experimental situation.

name: food preferences
query: Query: food preferences [SEP] Food preferences is the selection of one food over another.

name: food storage
query: Query: food storage [SEP] Food storage is keeping food for later consumption.

name: forensic genetics
query: Query: forensic genetics [SEP] Forensic genetics is the application of genetic analyses and molecular diagnostic techniques to legal matters and crime analysis.

name: forensic psychology
query: Query: forensic psychology [SEP] Forensic psychology is a specialty in professional psychology characterized by activities primarily intended to provide professional psychological expertise within the judicial and legal systems.

name: foster home care
query: Query: foster home care [SEP] Foster home care is families who care for neglected children or patients unable to care for themselves.

name: foundations
query: Query: foundations [SEP] Foundations is organizations established by endowments with provision for future maintenance.

name: fractionation , field flow
query: Query: fractionation , field flow [SEP] Field flow fractionation is separation of molecules and particles by a simultaneous action of carrier liquid flow and focusing field forces (electrical, sedimentation, or thermal), without a stationary phase.

name: fracture dislocation
query: Query: fracture dislocation [SEP] Fracture dislocation is fracture of a bone near an articulation with concomitant dislocation of that joint.

name: fractures , closed
query: Query: fractures , closed [SEP] Closed fractures is fractures in which the break in bone is not accompanied by an external wound.

name: fractures , compression
query: Query: fractures , compression [SEP] Compression fractures is crumbling or smashing of cancellous bone by forces acting parallel to the long axis of bone. It is applied particularly to vertebral body fractures (spinal fractures). (Blauvelt and Nelson, a Manual of Orthopedic Terminology, 1994, p4)

name: fractures , open
query: Query: fractures , open [SEP] Open fractures is fractures in which there is an external wound communicating with the break of the bone.

name: fragile x mental retardation protein
query: Query: fragile x mental retardation protein [SEP] Fragile x mental retardation protein is a RNA-binding protein that is found predominately in the cytoplasm. It helps regulate genetic translation in neurons and is absent or under-expressed in fragile x syndrome.

name: frail elderly
query: Query: frail elderly [SEP] Frail elderly is older adults or aged individuals who are lacking in general strength and are unusually susceptible to disease or to other infirmity.

name: fraud
query: Query: fraud [SEP] Fraud is exploitation through misrepresentation of the facts or concealment of the purposes of the exploiter.

name: functional food
query: Query: functional food [SEP] Functional food is components of the usual diet that may provide health benefits beyond basic nutrients. Examples of functional foods include soy, nuts, chocolate, and cranberries (From nccam Backgrounder, March 2004, p3).

name: fungal polysaccharides
query: Query: fungal polysaccharides [SEP] Fungal polysaccharides is cell wall components constituting a polysaccharide core found in fungi. They may act as antigens or structural substrates.

name: fuzzy logic
query: Query: fuzzy logic [SEP] Fuzzy logic is approximate, quantitative reasoning that is concerned with the linguistic ambiguity which exists in natural or synthetic language. At its core are variables such as good, bad, and young as well as modifiers such as more, less, and very. These ordinary terms represent fuzzy sets in a particular problem. Fuzzy logic plays a key role in many medical expert systems.

name: gait ataxia
query: Query: gait ataxia [SEP] Gait ataxia is impairment of the ability to coordinate the movements required for normal ambulation (walking) which may result from impairments of motor function or sensory feedback. This condition may be associated with brain diseases (including cerebellar diseases and basal ganglia diseases); spinal cord diseases; or peripheral nervous system diseases.

name: gamma rhythm
query: Query: gamma rhythm [SEP] Gamma rhythm is brain waves characterized by a relatively high voltage or amplitude and a frequency of approximately 30-100 Hz. They are primarily observed during network engagement and sensory processing activities, during both waking and sleeping states.

name: gas poisoning
query: Query: gas poisoning [SEP] Gas poisoning is poisoning that results from exposure to gases such as carbon monoxide; noble gases; oxygen; or natural gas.

name: gastric lavage
query: Query: gastric lavage [SEP] Gastric lavage is medical procedure involving the emptying of contents in the stomach through the use of a tube inserted through the nose or mouth. It is performed to remove poisons or relieve pressure due to intestinal blockages or during surgery.

name: gastric outlet obstruction
query: Query: gastric outlet obstruction [SEP] Gastric outlet obstruction is the hindering of output from the stomach into the small intestine. This obstruction may be of mechanical or functional origin such as edema from peptic ulcer; neoplasms; foreign bodies; or aging.

name: gb virus c
query: Query: gb virus c [SEP] Gb virus c is a species of virus in the family flaviviridae. It is genetically heterogeneous, of human origin, and transmitted by blood or blood products. Despite its alternate name (Hepatitis g virus), its pathogenicity remains controversial.

name: gene conversion
query: Query: gene conversion [SEP] Gene conversion is the asymmetrical segregation of genes during replication which leads to the production of non-reciprocal recombinant strands and the apparent conversion of one allele into another. Thus, e.g., the meiotic products of an Aa individual may be AAAa or aaaA instead of AAaa, i.e., the a allele has been converted into the a allele or vice versa.

name: gene drive technology
query: Query: gene drive technology [SEP] Gene drive technology is the techniques involved in creating and inserting synthetic selfish genetic elements called gene drives. Gene drives carry a "payload gene" and are designed to increase in frequency in the population over time, eventually to all members of the population.

name: gene products , env
query: Query: gene products , env [SEP] Env gene products is retroviral proteins, often glycosylated, coded by the envelope (env) gene. They are usually synthesized as protein precursors (polyproteins) and later cleaved into the final viral envelope glycoproteins by a viral protease.

name: gene products , gag
query: Query: gene products , gag [SEP] Gag gene products is proteins coded by the retroviral gag gene. The products are usually synthesized as protein precursors or polyproteins, which are then cleaved by viral proteases to yield the final products. Many of the final products are associated with the nucleoprotein core of the virion. gag is short for group-specific antigen.

name: gene products , pol
query: Query: gene products , pol [SEP] Pol gene products is retroviral proteins coded by the pol gene. They are usually synthesized as a protein precursor (polyproteins) and later cleaved into final products that include reverse transcriptase, endonuclease/integrase, and viral protease. Sometimes they are synthesized as a gag-pol fusion protein (fusion proteins, gag-pol). pol is short for polymerase, the enzyme class of reverse transcriptase.

name: genes , developmental
query: Query: genes , developmental [SEP] Developmental genes is genes that determine the fate of a cell or cells in a region of the embryo during embryonic development.

name: genes , env
query: Query: genes , env [SEP] Env genes is dna sequences that form the coding region for the viral envelope (env) proteins in retroviruses. The env genes contain a cis-acting rna target sequence for the rev protein (= gene products, rev), termed the rev-responsive element (rre).

name: genes , mitochondrial
query: Query: genes , mitochondrial [SEP] Mitochondrial genes is genes that are located on the mitochondrial dna. Mitochondrial inheritance is often referred to as maternal inheritance but should be differentiated from maternal inheritance that is transmitted chromosomally.

name: genes , pol
query: Query: genes , pol [SEP] Pol genes is dna sequences that form the coding region for retroviral enzymes including reverse transcriptase, protease, and endonuclease/integrase. "pol" is short for polymerase, the enzyme class of reverse transcriptase.

name: genes , reporter
query: Query: genes , reporter [SEP] Reporter genes is genes whose expression is easily detectable and therefore used to study promoter activity at many positions in a target genome. In recombinant dna technology, these genes may be attached to a promoter region of interest.

name: genetic association studies
query: Query: genetic association studies [SEP] Genetic association studies is the analysis of a sequence such as a region of a chromosome, a haplotype, a gene, or an allele for its involvement in controlling the phenotype of a specific trait, metabolic pathway, or disease.

name: genetic drift
query: Query: genetic drift [SEP] Genetic drift is the fluctuation of the allele frequency from one generation to the next.

name: genetic heterogeneity
query: Query: genetic heterogeneity [SEP] Genetic heterogeneity is the presence of apparently similar characters for which the genetic evidence indicates that different genes or different genetic mechanisms are involved in different pedigrees. In clinical settings genetic heterogeneity refers to the presence of a variety of genetic defects which cause the same disease, often due to mutations at different loci on the same gene, a finding common to many human diseases including alzheimer disease; cystic fibrosis; lipoprotein lipase deficiency, familial; and polycystic kidney diseases. (Rieger, et al., Glossary of Genetics: Classical and Molecular, 5th ed; Segen, Dictionary of Modern Medicine, 1992)

name: genetic load
query: Query: genetic load [SEP] Genetic load is the relative amount by which the average fitness of a population is lowered, due to the presence of genes that decrease survival, compared to the genotype with maximum or optimal fitness. (From Rieger et al., Glossary of Genetics: Classical and Molecular, 5th ed)

name: genetic speciation
query: Query: genetic speciation [SEP] Genetic speciation is the splitting of an ancestral species into daughter species that coexist in time (King, Dictionary of Genetics, 6th ed). Causal factors may include geographic isolation, habitat geometry, migration, reproductive isolation, random genetic drift and mutation.

name: genome , mitochondrial
query: Query: genome , mitochondrial [SEP] Mitochondrial genome is the genetic complement of mitochondria as represented in their dna.

name: genome size
query: Query: genome size [SEP] Genome size is the amount of dna (or rna) in one copy of a genome.

name: giant cell tumor of tendon sheath
query: Query: giant cell tumor of tendon sheath [SEP] Giant cell tumor of tendon sheath is a tumor arising in the synovial membrane; synovial bursa; or tendon sheath. It is characterized by OSTEOCLAST-like giant cells; foam cells; pigmented HEMOSIDERIN-laden macrophages and inflammatory infiltrate. It is classified either as diffuse or localized tenosynovitis.

name: glasgow outcome scale
query: Query: glasgow outcome scale [SEP] Glasgow outcome scale is a scale that assesses the outcome of serious craniocerebral injuries, based on the level of regained social functioning.

name: glomerular basement membrane
query: Query: glomerular basement membrane [SEP] Glomerular basement membrane is the layer of extracellular matrix that lies between the endothelium of the glomerular capillaries and the podocytes of the inner or visceral layer of the bowman capsule. It is the product of these two cell types. It acts as a physical barrier and an ion-selective filter.

name: glomerular filtration rate
query: Query: glomerular filtration rate [SEP] Glomerular filtration rate is the volume of water filtered out of plasma through glomerular capillary walls into Bowman's capsules per unit of time. It is considered to be equivalent to inulin clearance.

name: glucocorticoids
query: Query: glucocorticoids [SEP] Glucocorticoids is a group of corticosteroids that affect carbohydrate metabolism (gluconeogenesis, liver glycogen deposition, elevation of blood sugar), inhibit adrenocorticotropic hormone secretion, and possess pronounced anti-inflammatory activity. They also play a role in fat and protein metabolism, maintenance of arterial blood pressure, alteration of the connective tissue response to injury, reduction in the number of circulating lymphocytes, and functioning of the central nervous system.

name: glue proteins , drosophila
query: Query: glue proteins , drosophila [SEP] Drosophila glue proteins is glycosylated proteins which are part of the salivary glue that Drosophila larvae secrete as a means of fixing themselves to an external substrate for the duration of the pre-pupal and pupal period.

name: glutamine
query: Query: glutamine [SEP] Glutamine is a non-essential amino acid present abundantly throughout the body and is involved in many metabolic processes. It is synthesized from glutamic acid and ammonia. It is the principal carrier of nitrogen in the body and is an important energy source for many cells.

name: glutathione disulfide
query: Query: glutathione disulfide [SEP] Glutathione disulfide is a glutathione dimer formed by a disulfide bond between the cysteine sulfhydryl side chains during the course of being oxidized.

name: glycine plasma membrane transport proteins
query: Query: glycine plasma membrane transport proteins [SEP] Glycine plasma membrane transport proteins is a family of sodium chloride-dependent neurotransmitter symporters that transport the amino acid glycine. They differ from glycine receptors, which signal cellular responses to glycine. They are located primarily on the plasma membrane of neurons; glial cells; epithelial cells; and red blood cells where they remove inhibitory neurotransmitter glycine from the extracellular space.

name: glycogen storage disease type viii
query: Query: glycogen storage disease type viii [SEP] Glycogen storage disease type viii is an x-linked recessive hepatic glycogen storage disease resulting from lack of expression of phosphorylase-b-kinase activity. Symptoms are relatively mild; hepatomegaly, increased liver glycogen, and decreased leukocyte phosphorylase are present. Liver shrinkage occurs in response to glucagon.

name: glycogen synthase kinase 3 beta
query: Query: glycogen synthase kinase 3 beta [SEP] Glycogen synthase kinase 3 beta is a glycogen synthase kinase-3 type enzyme that functions in energy metabolism; embryonic development; and neurogenesis. It is also involved in protein biosynthesis and regulates cell growth and proliferation as a component of the wnt signaling pathway and other signaling pathways. Certain polymorphisms in the gsk3b gene have been associated with parkinson disease; alzheimer disease; and bipolar disorder.

name: gold isotopes
query: Query: gold isotopes [SEP] Gold isotopes is stable gold atoms that have the same atomic number as the element gold, but differ in atomic weight. Au-197 is a stable isotope.

name: government publications as topic
query: Query: government publications as topic [SEP] Government publications as topic is works about publications issued by local, regional, or national governments or by their agencies or subdivisions.

name: graphite
query: Query: graphite [SEP] Graphite is an allotropic form of carbon that is used in pencils, as a lubricant, and in matches and explosives. It is obtained by mining and its dust can cause lung irritation.

name: grassland
query: Query: grassland [SEP] Grassland is an ecosystem dominated by grasses (poaceae) with few trees or shrubs.

name: gray platelet syndrome
query: Query: gray platelet syndrome [SEP] Gray platelet syndrome is a rare, inherited platelet disorder characterized by a selective deficiency in the number and contents of platelet alpha-granules. It is associated with thrombocytopenia, enlarged platelets, and prolonged bleeding time.

name: greenhouse effect
query: Query: greenhouse effect [SEP] Greenhouse effect is the effect of greenhouse gases and the resulting increase in world temperatures. The predicted health effects of such long-term climatic change include increased incidence of respiratory, water-borne, and vector-borne diseases.

name: grounded theory
query: Query: grounded theory [SEP] Grounded theory is the generation of theories from analysis of empirical data.

name: group structure
