query: Query: group structure [SEP] Group structure is the informal or formal organization of a group of people based on a network of personal relationships which is influenced by the size and composition, etc., of the group.

name: growth differentiation factor 1
query: Query: growth differentiation factor 1 [SEP] Growth differentiation factor 1 is a growth differentiation factor that plays a role in the genesis of left-right asymmetry during vertebrate development. Evidence for this role is seen in mice where loss of growth differentiation factor 1 function results in right-left isomerism of visceral organs. In humans heterozygous loss of growth differentiation factor 1 function has been associated with congenital heart defects and transposition of great vessels.

name: growth differentiation factor 6
query: Query: growth differentiation factor 6 [SEP] Growth differentiation factor 6 is a growth differentiation factor that plays a role in the neural differentiation, specifically in the retinal development of the eye.

name: guinea
query: Query: guinea [SEP] Guinea is a republic in western Africa, south of senegal and mali, east of guinea-bissau. Its capital is Conakry.

name: gulf of mexico
query: Query: gulf of mexico [SEP] Gulf of mexico is a body of water located at the southeastern corner of North America. It is bordered by the states to the north of Florida, Alabama, Mississippi, Louisiana, Texas; by five Mexican states to the west: Tamaulipas, Veracruz, Tabasco, Campeche, Yucatan; and by Cuba to the southeast.

name: gun violence
query: Query: gun violence [SEP] Gun violence is violence using any type of firearm.

name: hair cells , auditory , inner
query: Query: hair cells , auditory , inner [SEP] Inner auditory hair cells is auditory sensory cells of organ of Corti, usually placed in one row medially to the core of spongy bone (the modiolus). Inner hair cells are in fewer numbers than the outer auditory hair cells, and their stereocilia are approximately twice as thick as those of the outer hair cells.

name: hair cells , vestibular
query: Query: hair cells , vestibular [SEP] Vestibular hair cells is sensory cells in the acoustic maculae with their apical stereocilia embedded in a gelatinous otolithic membrane. These hair cells are stimulated by the movement of otolithic membrane, and impulses are transmitted via the vestibular nerve to the brain stem. Hair cells in the saccule and those in the utricle sense linear acceleration in vertical and horizontal directions, respectively.

name: hair diseases
query: Query: hair diseases [SEP] Hair diseases is diseases affecting the orderly growth and persistence of hair.

name: hair removal
query: Query: hair removal [SEP] Hair removal is methods used to remove unwanted facial and body hair.

name: hand bones
query: Query: hand bones [SEP] Hand bones is the carpal bones; metacarpal bones; and finger phalanges. In each hand there are eight carpal bones, five metacarpal bones, and 14 phalanges.

name: hazard analysis and critical control points
query: Query: hazard analysis and critical control points [SEP] Hazard analysis and critical control points is a system of safety management (abbreviated haccp) applied mainly to the food industry. It involves the analysis and control of biological, chemical, and physical hazards, from raw material production, procurement and handling, to manufacturing, distribution and consumption of finished products.

name: headache disorders , secondary
query: Query: headache disorders , secondary [SEP] Secondary headache disorders is conditions with headache symptom that can be attributed to a variety of causes including brain vascular disorders; wounds and injuries; infection; drug use or its withdrawal.

name: head protective devices
query: Query: head protective devices [SEP] Head protective devices is personal devices for protection of heads from impact, penetration from falling and flying objects, and from limited electric shock and burn.

name: health information exchange
query: Query: health information exchange [SEP] Health information exchange is organizational framework for the dissemination of electronic healthcare information or clinical data, across health-related institutions and systems. Its overall purpose is to enhance patient care.

name: health planning support
query: Query: health planning support [SEP] Health planning support is financial resources provided for activities related to health planning and development.

name: health planning technical assistance
query: Query: health planning technical assistance [SEP] Health planning technical assistance is the provision of expert assistance in developing health planning programs, plans as technical materials, etc., as requested by Health Systems Agencies or other health planning organizations.

name: health services , indigenous
query: Query: health services , indigenous [SEP] Indigenous health services is health care provided to specific cultural or tribal peoples which incorporates local customs, beliefs, and taboos.

name: health services misuse
query: Query: health services misuse [SEP] Health services misuse is excessive, under or unnecessary utilization of health services by patients or physicians.

name: health transition
query: Query: health transition [SEP] Health transition is demographic and epidemiologic changes that have occurred in the last five decades in many developing countries and that are characterized by major growth in the number and proportion of middle-aged and elderly persons and in the frequency of the diseases that occur in these age groups. The health transition is the result of efforts to improve maternal and child health via primary care and outreach services and such efforts have been responsible for a decrease in the birth rate; reduced maternal mortality; improved preventive services; reduced infant mortality, and the increased life expectancy that defines the transition. (From Ann Intern Med 1992 Mar 15;116(6):499-504)

name: hearing loss , bilateral
query: Query: hearing loss , bilateral [SEP] Bilateral hearing loss is partial hearing loss in both ears.

name: hearing loss , central
query: Query: hearing loss , central [SEP] Central hearing loss is hearing loss due to disease of the auditory pathways (in the central nervous system) which originate in the cochlear nuclei of the pons and then ascend bilaterally to the midbrain, the thalamus, and then the auditory cortex in the temporal lobe. Bilateral lesions of the auditory pathways are usually required to cause central hearing loss. Cortical deafness refers to loss of hearing due to bilateral auditory cortex lesions. Unilateral brain stem lesions involving the cochlear nuclei may result in unilateral hearing loss.

name: hearing loss , sudden
query: Query: hearing loss , sudden [SEP] Sudden hearing loss is sensorineural hearing loss which develops suddenly over a period of hours or a few days. It varies in severity from mild to total deafness. Sudden deafness can be due to head trauma, vascular diseases, infections, or can appear without obvious cause or warning.

name: heart neoplasms
query: Query: heart neoplasms [SEP] Heart neoplasms is tumors in any part of the heart. They include primary cardiac tumors and metastatic tumors to the heart. Their interference with normal cardiac functions can cause a wide variety of symptoms including heart failure; cardiac arrhythmias; or embolism.

name: heating
query: Query: heating [SEP] Heating is the application of heat to raise the temperature of the environment, ambient or local, or the systems for accomplishing this effect. It is distinguished from heat, the physical property and principle of physics.

name: heat stroke
query: Query: heat stroke [SEP] Heat stroke is a condition caused by the failure of body to dissipate heat in an excessively hot environment or during physical exertion in a hot environment. Contrast to heat exhaustion, the body temperature in heat stroke patient is dangerously high with red, hot skin accompanied by delusions; convulsions; or coma. It can be a life-threatening emergency and is most common in infants and the elderly.

name: helium
query: Query: helium [SEP] Helium is a noble gas with the atomic symbol He, atomic number 2, and atomic weight 4.003. It is a colorless, odorless, tasteless gas that is not combustible and does not support combustion. It was first detected in the sun and is now obtained from natural gas. Medically it is used as a diluent for other gases, being especially useful with oxygen in the treatment of certain cases of respiratory obstruction, and as a vehicle for general anesthetics.

name: helsinki declaration
query: Query: helsinki declaration [SEP] Helsinki declaration is an international agreement of the World Medical Association which offers guidelines for conducting experiments using human subjects. It was adopted in 1962 and revised by the 18th World Medical Assembly at Helsinki, Finland in 1964. Subsequent revisions were made in 1975, 1983, 1989, and 1996. (From Encyclopedia of Bioethics, rev ed, 1995)

name: hematoma , epidural , cranial
query: Query: hematoma , epidural , cranial [SEP] Cranial epidural hematoma is accumulation of blood in the epidural space between the skull and the dura mater, often as a result of bleeding from the meningeal arteries associated with a temporal or parietal bone fracture. Epidural hematoma tends to expand rapidly, compressing the dura and underlying brain. Clinical features may include headache; vomiting; hemiparesis; and impaired mental function.

name: hematoma , epidural , spinal
query: Query: hematoma , epidural , spinal [SEP] Spinal epidural hematoma is a rare epidural hematoma in the spinal epidural space, usually due to a vascular malformation (central nervous system vascular malformations) or trauma. Spontaneous spinal epidural hematoma is a neurologic emergency due to a rapidly evolving compressive myelopathy.

name: hepatic infarction
query: Query: hepatic infarction [SEP] Hepatic infarction is formation of infarct resulting from obstruction of hepatic artery and/or portal vein most often after liver transplantation or hepatobiliary surgery.

name: hepatitis a antibodies
query: Query: hepatitis a antibodies [SEP] Hepatitis a antibodies is antibodies to the hepatitis a antigens including antibodies to envelope, core, and non-structural proteins.

name: hepatitis a antigens
query: Query: hepatitis a antigens [SEP] Hepatitis a antigens is antigens produced by various strains of hepatitis a virus such as the human hepatitis a virus (hepatitis a virus, human).

name: hepatitis b core antigens
query: Query: hepatitis b core antigens [SEP] Hepatitis b core antigens is the hepatitis b antigen within the core of the Dane particle, the infectious hepatitis virion.

name: hepatitis c antibodies
query: Query: hepatitis c antibodies [SEP] Hepatitis c antibodies is antibodies to the hepatitis c antigens including antibodies to envelope, core, and non-structural proteins.

name: hepatitis delta antigens
query: Query: hepatitis delta antigens [SEP] Hepatitis delta antigens is antigens produced by various strains of hepatitis d virus.

name: hepatitis delta virus
query: Query: hepatitis delta virus [SEP] Hepatitis delta virus is a defective virus, containing particles of rna nucleoprotein in virion-like form, present in patients with acute hepatitis b and chronic hepatitis. It requires the presence of a hepadnavirus for full replication. This is the lone species in the genus Deltavirus.

name: hepatocyte growth factor
query: Query: hepatocyte growth factor [SEP] Hepatocyte growth factor is multifunctional growth factor which regulates both cell growth and cell motility. It exerts a strong mitogenic effect on hepatocytes and primary epithelial cells. Its receptor is proto-oncogene proteins c-met.

name: hepatocyte nuclear factor 6
query: Query: hepatocyte nuclear factor 6 [SEP] Hepatocyte nuclear factor 6 is a onecut transcription factor that regulates expression of genes involved in embryonic development of the pancreas and liver.

name: hepatocytes
query: Query: hepatocytes [SEP] Hepatocytes is the main structural component of the liver. They are specialized epithelial cells that are organized into interconnected plates called lobules.

name: herbal medicine
query: Query: herbal medicine [SEP] Herbal medicine is the study of medicines derived from botanical sources.

name: hereditary breast and ovarian cancer syndrome
query: Query: hereditary breast and ovarian cancer syndrome [SEP] Hereditary breast and ovarian cancer syndrome is autosomal dominant hereditary cancer syndrome in which a mutation most often in either brca1 or brca2 is associated with a significantly increased risk for breast and ovarian cancers.

name: hernia , inguinal
query: Query: hernia , inguinal [SEP] Inguinal hernia is an abdominal hernia with an external bulge in the groin region. It can be classified by the location of herniation. Indirect inguinal hernias occur through the internal inguinal ring. Direct inguinal hernias occur through defects in the abdominal wall (transversalis fascia) in Hesselbach's triangle. The former type is commonly seen in children and young adults; the latter in adults.

name: hip dislocation , congenital
query: Query: hip dislocation , congenital [SEP] Congenital hip dislocation is congenital dislocation of the hip generally includes subluxation of the femoral head, acetabular dysplasia, and complete dislocation of the femoral head from the true acetabulum. This condition occurs in approximately 1 in 1000 live births and is more common in females than in males.

name: histamine agonists
query: Query: histamine agonists [SEP] Histamine agonists is drugs that bind to and activate histamine receptors. Although they have been suggested for a variety of clinical applications histamine agonists have so far been more widely used in research than therapeutically.

name: histological techniques
query: Query: histological techniques [SEP] Histological techniques is methods of preparing tissue for examination and study of the origin, structure, function, or pathology.

name: historical trauma
query: Query: historical trauma [SEP] Historical trauma is clinical distress among descendants of survivors of mass trauma, as if they had suffered through the same extreme historic circumstances. Symptoms may persist through generations.

name: history of medicine
query: Query: history of medicine [SEP] History of medicine is study of past events and development in the field of Medicine.

name: history of pharmacy
query: Query: history of pharmacy [SEP] History of pharmacy is study of the origins and development of the field of pharmacy.

name: hiv protease inhibitors
query: Query: hiv protease inhibitors [SEP] Hiv protease inhibitors is inhibitors of hiv protease, an enzyme required for production of proteins needed for viral assembly.

name: home care agencies
query: Query: home care agencies [SEP] Home care agencies is public or private organizations that provide, either directly or through arrangements with other organizations, home health services in the patient's home. (Hospital Administration Terminology, 2d ed)

name: homocysteine
query: Query: homocysteine [SEP] Homocysteine is a thiol-containing amino acid formed by a demethylation of methionine.

name: hormonal contraception
query: Query: hormonal contraception [SEP] Hormonal contraception is contraceptive methods that utilize hormonal contraceptive agents.

name: hospital charges
query: Query: hospital charges [SEP] Hospital charges is the prices a hospital sets for its services. hospital costs (the direct and indirect expenses incurred by the hospital in providing the services) are one factor in the determination of hospital charges. Other factors may include, for example, profits, competition, and the necessity of recouping the costs of uncompensated care.

name: hospital communication systems
query: Query: hospital communication systems [SEP] Hospital communication systems is the transmission of messages to staff and patients within a hospital.

name: hospitals , animal
query: Query: hospitals , animal [SEP] Animal hospitals is facility for in-house medical care of animals.

name: hospitals , general
query: Query: hospitals , general [SEP] General hospitals is large hospitals with a resident medical staff which provides continuous care to maternity, surgical and medical patients.

name: hospitals , isolation
query: Query: hospitals , isolation [SEP] Isolation hospitals is hospitals designed or used to isolate or quarantine persons with communicable diseases.

name: hospitals , municipal
query: Query: hospitals , municipal [SEP] Municipal hospitals is hospitals controlled by the city government.

name: hospitals , pediatric
query: Query: hospitals , pediatric [SEP] Pediatric hospitals is special hospitals which provide care for ill children.

name: host factor 1 protein
query: Query: host factor 1 protein [SEP] Host factor 1 protein is an integration host factor that was originally identified as a bacterial protein required for the integration of bacteriophage q beta (allolevivirus). Its cellular function may be to regulate mRNA stability and processing in that it binds tightly to poly(A) rna and interferes with ribosome binding.

name: host microbial interactions
query: Query: host microbial interactions [SEP] Host microbial interactions is interactions between a host and microbe or microbiota.

name: human migration
query: Query: human migration [SEP] Human migration is dispersion or dislocation of people from their country of origin, either voluntarily or involuntarily.

name: hybrid renal replacement therapy
query: Query: hybrid renal replacement therapy [SEP] Hybrid renal replacement therapy is procedures involving non-continuous blood purification (e.g., dialysis, filtration or perfusion) via vascular access with settings for dialysate and blood flow rates and treatment duration settings hybrid between crrt technique and irrt technique.

name: hydrocarbons , acyclic
query: Query: hydrocarbons , acyclic [SEP] Acyclic hydrocarbons is organic compounds composed exclusively of carbon and hydrogen where no carbon atoms join to form a ring structure.

name: hydrogels
query: Query: hydrogels [SEP] Hydrogels is water swollen, rigid, 3-dimensional network of cross-linked, hydrophilic macromolecules, 20-95% water. They are used in paints, printing inks, foodstuffs, pharmaceuticals, and cosmetics. (Grant & Hackh's Chemical Dictionary, 5th ed)

name: hydrogen sulfide
query: Query: hydrogen sulfide [SEP] Hydrogen sulfide is a flammable, poisonous gas with a characteristic odor of rotten eggs. It is used in the manufacture of chemicals, in metallurgy, and as an analytical reagent. (From Merck Index, 11th ed)

name: hypertension , malignant
query: Query: hypertension , malignant [SEP] Malignant hypertension is a condition of markedly elevated blood pressure with diastolic pressure usually greater than 120 mm Hg. Malignant hypertension is characterized by widespread vascular damage, papilledema, retinopathy, hypertensive encephalopathy, and renal dysfunction.

name: hypotension , controlled
query: Query: hypotension , controlled [SEP] Controlled hypotension is procedure in which arterial blood pressure is intentionally reduced in order to control blood loss during surgery. This procedure is performed either pharmacologically or by pre-surgical removal of blood.

name: hypothalamus , middle
query: Query: hypothalamus , middle [SEP] Middle hypothalamus is middle portion of the hypothalamus containing the arcuate, dorsomedial, ventromedial nuclei, the tuber cinereum and the pituitary gland.

name: hypothalamus , posterior
query: Query: hypothalamus , posterior [SEP] Posterior hypothalamus is the part of the hypothalamus posterior to the middle region consisting of several nuclei including the medial maxillary nucleus, lateral mammillary nucleus, and posterior hypothalamic nucleus (posterior hypothalamic area). The posterior hypothalamic area is concerned with control of sympathetic responses and is sensitive to conditions of decreasing temperature and controls the mechanisms for the conservation and increased production of heat.

name: hysterectomy , vaginal
query: Query: hysterectomy , vaginal [SEP] Vaginal hysterectomy is removal of the uterus through the vagina.

name: iliac aneurysm
query: Query: iliac aneurysm [SEP] Iliac aneurysm is abnormal balloon- or sac-like dilatation in the wall of any one of the iliac arteries including the common, the internal, or the external iliac artery.

name: illness behavior
query: Query: illness behavior [SEP] Illness behavior is coordinate set of non-specific behavioral responses to non-psychiatric illness. These may include loss of appetite or libido; disinterest in activities of daily living; or withdrawal from social interaction.

name: imagery , psychotherapy
query: Query: imagery , psychotherapy [SEP] Psychotherapy imagery is the use of mental images produced by the imagination as a form of psychotherapy. It can be classified by the modality of its content: visual, verbal, auditory, olfactory, tactile, gustatory, or kinesthetic. Common themes derive from nature imagery (e.g., forests and mountains), water imagery (e.g., brooks and oceans), travel imagery, etc. Imagery is used in the treatment of mental disorders and in helping patients cope with other diseases. Imagery often forms a part of hypnosis, of autogenic training, of relaxation techniques, and of behavior therapy. (From Encyclopedia of Human Behavior, vol. 4, pp29-30, 1994)

name: immunity , heterologous
query: Query: immunity , heterologous [SEP] Heterologous immunity is the immunological phenomenon by which exposure to some organisms or vaccines can profoundly alter the host's response to subsequent exposure to unrelated (heterologous) organisms or vaccines.

name: immunization , secondary
query: Query: immunization , secondary [SEP] Secondary immunization is any immunization following a primary immunization and involving exposure to the same or a closely related antigen.

name: immunization schedule
query: Query: immunization schedule [SEP] Immunization schedule is schedule giving optimum times usually for primary and/or secondary immunization.

name: immunoglobulin switch region
query: Query: immunoglobulin switch region [SEP] Immunoglobulin switch region is a site located in the introns at the 5' end of each constant region segment of a immunoglobulin heavy-chain gene where recombination (or rearrangement) occur during immunoglobulin class switching. Ig switch regions are found on genes encoding all five classes (immunoglobulin isotypes) of immunoglobulin heavy chains.

name: immunological synapses
query: Query: immunological synapses [SEP] Immunological synapses is the interfaces between t-cells and antigen-presenting cells. Supramolecular organization of proteins takes place at these synapses involving various types of immune cells. Immunological synapses can have several functions including lymphocyte activation; enhancing, balancing, or terminating signaling; or directing cytokine secretion.

name: inappropriate adh syndrome
query: Query: inappropriate adh syndrome [SEP] Inappropriate adh syndrome is a condition of hyponatremia and renal salt loss attributed to overexpansion of body fluids resulting from sustained release of antidiuretic hormones which stimulates renal resorption of water. It is characterized by normal kidney function, high urine osmolality, low serum osmolality, and neurological dysfunction. Etiologies include ADH-producing neoplasms, injuries or diseases involving the hypothalamus, the pituitary gland, and the lung. This syndrome can also be drug-induced.

name: inclusion bodies , viral
query: Query: inclusion bodies , viral [SEP] Viral inclusion bodies is an area showing altered staining behavior in the nucleus or cytoplasm of a virus-infected cell. Some inclusion bodies represent "virus factories" in which viral nucleic acid or protein is being synthesized; others are merely artifacts of fixation and staining. One example, Negri bodies, are found in the cytoplasm or processes of nerve cells in animals that have died from rabies.

name: independent living
query: Query: independent living [SEP] Independent living is a housing and community arrangement that maximizes independence and self-determination.

name: indonesia
query: Query: indonesia [SEP] Indonesia is a republic stretching from the Indian Ocean east to New Guinea, comprising six main islands: Java, Sumatra, Bali, Kalimantan (the Indonesian portion of the island of Borneo), Sulawesi (formerly known as the Celebes) and Irian Jaya (the western part of New Guinea). Its capital is Djakarta. The ethnic groups living there are largely Chinese, Arab, Eurasian, Indian, and Pakistani; 85% of the peoples are of the Islamic faith.

name: industrial development
query: Query: industrial development [SEP] Industrial development is activity concerned with the planning and building of industries through manufacturing, provision of specialized services, and commerce.

name: infant , extremely low birth weight
query: Query: infant , extremely low birth weight [SEP] Extremely low birth weight infant is an infant whose weight at birth is less than 1000 grams (2.2 lbs), regardless of gestational age.

name: infant , small for gestational age
query: Query: infant , small for gestational age [SEP] Small for gestational age infant is an infant having a birth weight lower than expected for its gestational age.

name: inferior wall myocardial infarction
query: Query: inferior wall myocardial infarction [SEP] Inferior wall myocardial infarction is myocardial infarction in which the inferior wall of the heart is involved. It is often caused by occlusion of the right coronary artery.

name: infertility , female
query: Query: infertility , female [SEP] Female infertility is diminished or absent ability of a female to achieve conception.

name: information technology
query: Query: information technology [SEP] Information technology is interconnected system that is used in the automatic acquisition, storage, manipulation, movement, control, display, interchange, transmission, routing or reception of data or information, including computers, ancillary equipment, system software, support services, and related resources. (nal Agricultural Thesaurus)

name: information theory
query: Query: information theory [SEP] Information theory is an interdisciplinary study dealing with the transmission of messages or signals, or the communication of information. Information theory does not directly deal with meaning or content, but with physical representations that have meaning or content. It overlaps considerably with communication theory and cybernetics.

name: infusions , intravenous
query: Query: infusions , intravenous [SEP] Intravenous infusions is the long-term (minutes to hours) administration of a fluid into the vein through venipuncture, either by letting the fluid flow by gravity or by pumping it.

name: inhalation exposure
query: Query: inhalation exposure [SEP] Inhalation exposure is the exposure to potentially harmful chemical, physical, or biological agents by inhaling them.

name: inhibitor of differentiation protein 1
query: Query: inhibitor of differentiation protein 1 [SEP] Inhibitor of differentiation protein 1 is a helix-loop-helix MOTIF-containing negative regulator of basic helix-loop-helix transcription factors that blocks activation of cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor p16 and is de-regulated in a variety of neoplasms.

name: inhibitor of differentiation protein 2
query: Query: inhibitor of differentiation protein 2 [SEP] Inhibitor of differentiation protein 2 is a negative regulator of basic helix-loop-helix transcription factors. It plays a role in regulating immunoglobulin e expression.

name: inhibitor of growth protein 1
query: Query: inhibitor of growth protein 1 [SEP] Inhibitor of growth protein 1 is a nuclear protein and tumor suppressor that contains a C-terminal phd zinc finger. It is expressed in different isoforms in various tissues and interacts with tumor suppressor protein p53 to negatively regulate cell growth. Reduced expression and chromosomal rearrangements of the ing1 gene are associated with different cancers including head and neck neoplasms.

name: inhibitory postsynaptic potentials
query: Query: inhibitory postsynaptic potentials [SEP] Inhibitory postsynaptic potentials is hyperpolarization of membrane potentials at the synaptic membranes of target neurons during neurotransmission. They are local changes which diminish responsiveness to excitatory signals.

name: injections , intraperitoneal
query: Query: injections , intraperitoneal [SEP] Intraperitoneal injections is forceful administration into the peritoneal cavity of liquid medication, nutrient, or other fluid through a hollow needle piercing the abdominal wall.

name: institutional management teams
query: Query: institutional management teams [SEP] Institutional management teams is administrator-selected management groups who are responsible for making decisions pertaining to the provision of integrated direction for various institutional functions.

name: insulin antibodies
query: Query: insulin antibodies [SEP] Insulin antibodies is antibodies specific to insulin.

name: insurance , dental
query: Query: insurance , dental [SEP] Dental insurance is insurance providing coverage for dental care.

name: insurance , psychiatric
query: Query: insurance , psychiatric [SEP] Psychiatric insurance is insurance providing benefits to cover part or all of the psychiatric care.

name: insurance , vision
query: Query: insurance , vision [SEP] Vision insurance is insurance providing coverage for vision care.

name: insurance benefits
query: Query: insurance benefits [SEP] Insurance benefits is payments or services provided under stated circumstances under the terms of an insurance policy. In prepayment programs, benefits are the services the programs will provide at defined locations and to the extent needed.

name: insurance pools
query: Query: insurance pools [SEP] Insurance pools is an organization of insurers or reinsurers through which particular types of risk are shared or pooled. The risk of high loss by a particular insurance company is transferred to the group as a whole (the insurance pool) with premiums, losses, and expenses shared in agreed amounts.

name: integrated advanced information management systems
query: Query: integrated advanced information management systems [SEP] Integrated advanced information management systems is a concept, developed in 1983 under the aegis of and supported by the National Library of Medicine under the name of Integrated Academic Information Management Systems, to provide professionals in academic health sciences centers and health sciences institutions with convenient access to an integrated and comprehensive network of knowledge. It addresses a wide cross-section of users from administrators and faculty to students and clinicians and has applications to planning, clinical and managerial decision-making, teaching, and research. It provides access to various types of clinical, management, educational, etc., databases, as well as to research and bibliographic databases. In August 1992 the name was changed from Integrated Academic Information Management Systems to Integrated Advanced Information Management Systems to reflect use beyond the academic milieu.

name: interferon regulatory factors
query: Query: interferon regulatory factors [SEP] Interferon regulatory factors is a family of transcription factors that share an N-terminal helix-turn-helix motif and bind INTERFERON-inducible promoters to control gene expression. irf proteins bind specific dna sequences such as interferon-stimulated response elements, interferon regulatory elements, and the interferon consensus sequence.

name: intermediate filaments
query: Query: intermediate filaments [SEP] Intermediate filaments is cytoplasmic filaments intermediate in diameter (about 10 nanometers) between the microfilaments and the microtubules. They may be composed of any of a number of different proteins and form a ring around the cell nucleus.

name: intracranial aneurysm
query: Query: intracranial aneurysm [SEP] Intracranial aneurysm is abnormal outpouching in the wall of intracranial blood vessels. Most common are the saccular (berry) aneurysms located at branch points in circle of willis at the base of the brain. Vessel rupture results in subarachnoid hemorrhage or intracranial hemorrhages. Giant aneurysms (>2.5 cm in diameter) may compress adjacent structures, including the oculomotor nerve. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p841)

name: intracranial embolism
query: Query: intracranial embolism [SEP] Intracranial embolism is blocking of a blood vessel in the skull by an embolus which can be a blood clot (thrombus) or other undissolved material in the blood stream. Most emboli are of cardiac origin and are associated with heart diseases. Other non-cardiac sources of emboli are usually associated with vascular diseases.

name: intracranial pressure
query: Query: intracranial pressure [SEP] Intracranial pressure is pressure within the cranial cavity. It is influenced by brain mass, the circulatory system, csf dynamics, and skull rigidity.

name: intraocular lymphoma
query: Query: intraocular lymphoma [SEP] Intraocular lymphoma is a form of malignant cancer which occurs within the eyeball.

name: intraoperative awareness
query: Query: intraoperative awareness [SEP] Intraoperative awareness is occurence of a patient becoming conscious during a procedure performed under general anesthesia and subsequently having recall of these events. (From Anesthesiology 2006, 104(4): 847-64.)

name: intrauterine devices
query: Query: intrauterine devices [SEP] Intrauterine devices is contraceptive devices placed high in the uterine fundus.

name: introductory journal article
query: Query: introductory journal article [SEP] Introductory journal article is prefatory summary to a special issue or section of a journal devoted to a specific topic. This introductory text can be of varying length and substance.

name: intubation
query: Query: intubation [SEP] Intubation is introduction of a tube into a hollow organ to restore or maintain patency if obstructed. It is differentiated from catheterization in that the insertion of a catheter is usually performed for the introducing or withdrawing of fluids from the body.

name: isometric contraction
query: Query: isometric contraction [SEP] Isometric contraction is muscular contractions characterized by increase in tension without change in length.

name: juvenile hormones
query: Query: juvenile hormones [SEP] Juvenile hormones is compounds, either natural or synthetic, which block development of the growing insect.

name: kidney failure , chronic
query: Query: kidney failure , chronic [SEP] Chronic kidney failure is the end-stage of chronic renal insufficiency. It is characterized by the severe irreversible kidney damage (as measured by the level of proteinuria) and the reduction in glomerular filtration rate to less than 15 ml per min (Kidney Foundation: Kidney Disease Outcome Quality Initiative, 2002). These patients generally require hemodialysis or kidney transplantation.

name: kidney tubular necrosis , acute
query: Query: kidney tubular necrosis , acute [SEP] Acute kidney tubular necrosis is acute kidney failure resulting from destruction of epithelial cells of the kidney tubules. It is commonly attributed to exposure to toxic agents or renal ischemia following severe trauma.

name: knee joint
query: Query: knee joint [SEP] Knee joint is a synovial hinge connection formed between the bones of the femur; tibia; and patella.

name: laboratory manual
query: Query: laboratory manual [SEP] Laboratory manual is work containing concise background information and directions for activities, including conducting experiments or diagnostic tests in the laboratory.

name: labor presentation
query: Query: labor presentation [SEP] Labor presentation is the position or orientation of the fetus at near term or during obstetric labor, determined by its relation to the spine of the mother and the birth canal. The normal position is a vertical, cephalic presentation with the fetal vertex flexed on the neck.

name: lactose tolerance test
query: Query: lactose tolerance test [SEP] Lactose tolerance test is a measure of a patient's ability to break down lactose.

name: lakes
query: Query: lakes [SEP] Lakes is inland bodies of still or slowly moving fresh water or salt water, larger than a pond, and supplied by rivers and streams.

name: laryngeal masks
query: Query: laryngeal masks [SEP] Laryngeal masks is a type of oropharyngeal airway that provides an alternative to endotracheal intubation and standard mask anesthesia in certain patients. It is introduced into the hypopharynx to form a seal around the larynx thus permitting spontaneous or positive pressure ventilation without penetration of the larynx or esophagus. It is used in place of a facemask in routine anesthesia. The advantages over standard mask anesthesia are better airway control, minimal anesthetic gas leakage, a secure airway during patient transport to the recovery area, and minimal postoperative problems.

name: laryngeal mucosa
query: Query: laryngeal mucosa [SEP] Laryngeal mucosa is the mucous lining of the larynx, consisting of various types of epithelial cells ranging from stratified squamous epithelium in the upper larynx to ciliated columnar epithelium in the rest of the larynx, mucous goblet cells, and glands containing both mucous and serous cells.

name: laryngeal muscles
query: Query: laryngeal muscles [SEP] Laryngeal muscles is the striated muscle groups which move the larynx as a whole or its parts, such as altering tension of the vocal cords, or size of the slit (rima glottidis).

name: lasers , gas
query: Query: lasers , gas [SEP] Gas lasers is lasers in which a gas lasing medium is stimulated to emit light by an electric current or high-frequency oscillator.

name: latent class analysis
query: Query: latent class analysis [SEP] Latent class analysis is a statistical algorithm used to analyze clusters of observed variables by constructing categorical unobserved or latent segment based on weighted analysis and the average probabilities. Such latent classes are used to infer variables whose relationships are not directly observed. In biomedical research, it is often used to categorize data that allows the determination of symptom clusters.

name: l cells
query: Query: l cells [SEP] L cells is a cultured line of c3h mouse fibroblasts that do not adhere to one another and do not express cadherins.

name: leadership
query: Query: leadership [SEP] Leadership is the function of directing or controlling the actions or attitudes of an individual or group with more or less willing acquiescence of the followers.

name: lecture
query: Query: lecture [SEP] Lecture is work consisting of speeches read or delivered before an audience or class, especially for instruction or to set forth some subject. They are differentiated from an address which are less didactic and more informational, entertaining, inspirational, or polemic. (From Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed)

name: lecture note
query: Query: lecture note [SEP] Lecture note is work consisting of notes taken at the delivery or reading of a speech before an audience or class, usually given to instruct. (From Random House Unabridged Dictionary, 2d ed)

name: legal case
query: Query: legal case [SEP] Legal case is work consisting of collections of law reports or the published reports of decided cases and documents or filings related to those cases.

name: legislation , dental
query: Query: legislation , dental [SEP] Dental legislation is laws and regulations pertaining to the field of dentistry, proposed for enactment or recently enacted by a legislative body.

name: legislation , food
query: Query: legislation , food [SEP] Food legislation is laws and regulations concerned with industrial processing and marketing of foods and beverages.

name: legislation , veterinary
query: Query: legislation , veterinary [SEP] Veterinary legislation is laws and regulations, pertaining to the field of veterinary medicine, proposed for enactment or enacted by a legislative body.

name: leucine
query: Query: leucine [SEP] Leucine is an essential branched-chain amino acid important for hemoglobin formation.

name: leukemia , experimental
query: Query: leukemia , experimental [SEP] Experimental leukemia is leukemia induced experimentally in animals by exposure to leukemogenic agents, such as viruses; radiation; or by transplantation of leukemic tissues.

name: leukemia , myeloid , acute
query: Query: leukemia , myeloid , acute [SEP] Acute myeloid leukemia is clonal expansion of myeloid blasts in bone marrow, blood, and other tissue. Myeloid leukemias develop from changes in cells that normally produce neutrophils; basophils; eosinophils; and monocytes.

name: leukemia inhibitory factor receptor alpha subunit
query: Query: leukemia inhibitory factor receptor alpha subunit [SEP] Leukemia inhibitory factor receptor alpha subunit is a receptor subunit that combines with cytokine receptor gp130 to form the dual specificity receptor for leukemia inhibitory factor and oncostatin m. The subunit is also a component of the ciliary neurotrophic factor receptor. Both membrane-bound and secreted isoforms of the receptor subunit exist due to alternative splicing of its mRNA. The secreted isoform is believed to act as an inhibitory receptor, while the membrane-bound form is a signaling receptor.

name: leukocyte rolling
query: Query: leukocyte rolling [SEP] Leukocyte rolling is movement of tethered, spherical leukocytes along the endothelial surface of the microvasculature. The tethering and rolling involves interaction with selectins and other adhesion molecules in both the endothelium and leukocyte. The rolling leukocyte then becomes activated by chemokines, flattens out, and firmly adheres to the endothelial surface in preparation for transmigration through the interendothelial cell junction. (From Abbas, Cellular and Molecular Immunology, 3rd ed)

name: lewis bases
query: Query: lewis bases [SEP] Lewis bases is any chemical species which acts as an electron-pair donor in a chemical bonding reaction with a lewis acid.

name: library administration
query: Query: library administration [SEP] Library administration is planning, organizing, staffing, direction, and control of libraries.

name: library automation
query: Query: library automation [SEP] Library automation is the use of automatic machines or processing devices in libraries. The automation may be applied to library administrative activities, office procedures, and delivery of library services to users.

name: library services
query: Query: library services [SEP] Library services is services offered to the library user. They include reference and circulation.

name: life history traits
query: Query: life history traits [SEP] Life history traits is morphological or behavioral traits influenced by various living conditions that a population encounters especially as it pertains to reproduction and survival of the population (see population dynamics) such as age at first reproductive event, number and size of offspring, and lifespan.

name: ligation
query: Query: ligation [SEP] Ligation is application of a ligature to tie a vessel or strangulate a part.

name: lightning injuries
query: Query: lightning injuries [SEP] Lightning injuries is accidental injuries caused by brief high-voltage electrical discharges during thunderstorms. Cardiopulmonary arrest, coma and other neurologic symptoms, myocardial necrosis, and dermal burns are common. Prompt treatment of the acute sequelae, including cardiopulmonary resuscitation, is indicated for survival.

name: likelihood functions
query: Query: likelihood functions [SEP] Likelihood functions is functions constructed from a statistical model and a set of observed data which give the probability of that data for various values of the unknown model parameters. Those parameter values that maximize the probability are the maximum likelihood estimates of the parameters.

name: linear energy transfer
query: Query: linear energy transfer [SEP] Linear energy transfer is rate of energy dissipation along the path of charged particles. In radiobiology and health physics, exposure is measured in kiloelectron volts per micrometer of tissue (keV/micrometer t).

name: lipid droplet associated proteins
query: Query: lipid droplet associated proteins [SEP] Lipid droplet associated proteins is proteins, such as perilipins, that localize to lipid droplets either transiently or constitutively.

name: lipid peroxidation
query: Query: lipid peroxidation [SEP] Lipid peroxidation is peroxidase catalyzed oxidation of lipids using hydrogen peroxide as an electron acceptor.

name: lipid regulating agents
query: Query: lipid regulating agents [SEP] Lipid regulating agents is substances that alter the metabolism of lipids.

name: literacy
query: Query: literacy [SEP] Literacy is ability to read and write.

name: liver extracts
query: Query: liver extracts [SEP] Liver extracts is extracts of liver tissue containing uncharacterized specific factors with specific activities; a soluble thermostable fraction of mammalian liver is used in the treatment of pernicious anemia.

name: logistic models
query: Query: logistic models [SEP] Logistic models is statistical models which describe the relationship between a qualitative dependent variable (that is, one which can take only certain discrete values, such as the presence or absence of a disease) and an independent variable. a common application is in epidemiology for estimating an individual's risk (probability of a disease) as a function of a given risk factor.

name: loss of function mutation
query: Query: loss of function mutation [SEP] Loss of function mutation is a mutation that causes a decrease in or elimination of a gene product's activity.

name: lung transplantation
query: Query: lung transplantation [SEP] Lung transplantation is the transference of either one or both of the lungs from one human or animal to another.

name: lymph
query: Query: lymph [SEP] Lymph is the interstitial fluid that is in the lymphatic system.

name: lymphatic metastasis
query: Query: lymphatic metastasis [SEP] Lymphatic metastasis is transfer of a neoplasm from its primary site to lymph nodes or to distant parts of the body by way of the lymphatic system.

name: macrophages , peritoneal
query: Query: macrophages , peritoneal [SEP] Peritoneal macrophages is mononuclear phagocytes derived from bone marrow precursors but resident in the peritoneum.

name: magnesium sulfate
query: Query: magnesium sulfate [SEP] Magnesium sulfate is a small colorless crystal used as an anticonvulsant, a cathartic, and an electrolyte replenisher in the treatment of pre-eclampsia and eclampsia. It causes direct inhibition of action potentials in myometrial muscle cells. Excitation and contraction are uncoupled, which decreases the frequency and force of contractions. (From ama Drug Evaluations Annual, 1992, p1083)

name: magnetic resonance imaging , interventional
query: Query: magnetic resonance imaging , interventional [SEP] Interventional magnetic resonance imaging is minimally invasive procedures guided with the aid of magnetic resonance imaging to visualize tissue structures.

name: magnets
query: Query: magnets [SEP] Magnets is objects that produce a magnetic field.

name: maintenance and engineering , hospital
query: Query: maintenance and engineering , hospital [SEP] Hospital maintenance and engineering is hospital department whose primary function is the upkeep and supervision of the buildings and grounds and the maintenance of hospital physical plant and equipment which requires engineering expertise.

name: mandatory reporting
query: Query: mandatory reporting [SEP] Mandatory reporting is a legal requirement that designated types of information acquired by professionals or institutions in the course of their work be reported to appropriate authorities.

name: manganese
query: Query: manganese [SEP] Manganese is a trace element with atomic symbol Mn, atomic number 25, and atomic weight 54.94. It is concentrated in cell mitochondria, mostly in the pituitary gland, liver, pancreas, kidney, and bone, influences the synthesis of mucopolysaccharides, stimulates hepatic synthesis of cholesterol and fatty acids, and is a cofactor in many enzymes, including arginase and alkaline phosphatase in the liver. (From ama Drug Evaluations Annual 1992, p2035)

name: manganese compounds
query: Query: manganese compounds [SEP] Manganese compounds is inorganic chemicals that contain manganese as an integral part of the molecule.

name: manure
query: Query: manure [SEP] Manure is accumulations of solid or liquid animal excreta usually from stables and barnyards with or without litter material. Its chief application is as a fertilizer. (From Webster's 3d ed)

name: marine toxins
query: Query: marine toxins [SEP] Marine toxins is toxic or poisonous substances elaborated by marine flora or fauna. They include also specific, characterized poisons or toxins for which there is no more specific heading, like those from poisonous fishes.

name: marital therapy
query: Query: marital therapy [SEP] Marital therapy is a form of psychotherapy involving both spouses and directed to improving the marital relationship.

name: masked hypertension
query: Query: masked hypertension [SEP] Masked hypertension is phenomenon where increased blood pressure readings taken in non-clinical settings (e.g., home blood pressure monitoring) do not replicate in clinical settings.

name: mass behavior
query: Query: mass behavior [SEP] Mass behavior is collective behavior of an aggregate of individuals giving the appearance of unity of attitude, feeling, and motivation.

name: mass vaccination
query: Query: mass vaccination [SEP] Mass vaccination is administration of a vaccine to large populations in order to elicit immunity.

name: mast cells
query: Query: mast cells [SEP] Mast cells is granulated cells that are found in almost all tissues, most abundantly in the skin and the gastrointestinal tract. Like the basophils, mast cells contain large amounts of histamine and heparin. Unlike basophils, mast cells normally remain in the tissues and do not circulate in the blood. Mast cells, derived from the bone marrow stem cells, are regulated by the stem cell factor.

name: maternal age
query: Query: maternal age [SEP] Maternal age is the age of the mother in pregnancy.

name: mathematical computing
query: Query: mathematical computing [SEP] Mathematical computing is computer-assisted interpretation and analysis of various mathematical functions related to a particular problem.

name: matrix attachment regions
query: Query: matrix attachment regions [SEP] Matrix attachment regions is regions of the chromatin or dna that bind to the nuclear matrix. They are found in intergenic dna, especially flanking the 5' ends of genes or clusters of genes. Many of the regions that have been isolated contain a bipartite sequence motif called the mar/sar recognition signature sequence that binds to matrix attachment region binding proteins.

name: maximal expiratory flow rate
query: Query: maximal expiratory flow rate [SEP] Maximal expiratory flow rate is the airflow rate measured during the first liter expired after the first 200 ml have been exhausted during a forced vital capacity determination. Common abbreviations are mefr, fef 200-1200, and fef 0.2-1.2.

name: maze learning
query: Query: maze learning [SEP] Maze learning is learning the correct route through a maze to obtain reinforcement. It is used for human or animal populations. (Thesaurus of Psychological Index Terms, 6th ed)

name: medical illustration
query: Query: medical illustration [SEP] Medical illustration is the field which deals with illustrative clarification of biomedical concepts, as in the use of diagrams and drawings. The illustration may be produced by hand, photography, computer, or other electronic or mechanical methods.

name: medical missions
query: Query: medical missions [SEP] Medical missions is travel by a group for the purpose of undertaking a health-care related project of short-term duration.

name: medical savings accounts
query: Query: medical savings accounts [SEP] Medical savings accounts is tax-exempt trusts or custodial accounts established by individuals with financial institutions for saving money for future medical expenses.

name: medical staff , hospital
query: Query: medical staff , hospital [SEP] Hospital medical staff is professional medical personnel approved to provide care to patients in a hospital.

name: medical tourism
query: Query: medical tourism [SEP] Medical tourism is travel to another country for the purpose of medical treatment or care.

name: medicare assignment
query: Query: medicare assignment [SEP] Medicare assignment is concept referring to the standardized fees for services rendered by health care providers, e.g., laboratories and physicians, and reimbursement for those services under Medicare Part b. It includes acceptance by the physician.

name: meeting abstract
query: Query: meeting abstract [SEP] Meeting abstract is individual abstracts of presentations at meetings, congresses, conferences, symposia, colloquia, seminars, workshops, round tables, and other professional gatherings.

name: melanoma , experimental
query: Query: melanoma , experimental [SEP] Experimental melanoma is experimentally induced tumor that produces melanin in animals to provide a model for studying human melanoma.

name: membrane fusion
query: Query: membrane fusion [SEP] Membrane fusion is the adherence and merging of cell membranes, intracellular membranes, or artificial membranes to each other or to viruses, parasites, or interstitial particles through a variety of chemical and physical processes.

name: meningitis , escherichia coli
query: Query: meningitis , escherichia coli [SEP] Escherichia coli meningitis is a form of gram-negative meningitis that tends to occur in neonates, in association with anatomical abnormalities (which feature communication between the meninges and cutaneous structures) or as opportunistic infections in association with immunologic deficiency syndromes. In premature neonates the clinical presentation may be limited to anorexia; vomiting; lethargy; or respiratory distress. Full-term infants may have as additional features fever; seizures; and bulging of the anterior fontanelle. (From Menkes, Textbook of Child Neurology, 5th ed, pp398-400)

name: mental healing
query: Query: mental healing [SEP] Mental healing is the use of mind to cure disease, particularly physical illness.

name: mentally ill persons
query: Query: mentally ill persons [SEP] Mentally ill persons is persons with psychiatric illnesses or diseases, particularly psychotic and severe mood disorders.

name: mental status schedule
query: Query: mental status schedule [SEP] Mental status schedule is standardized clinical interview used to assess current psychopathology by scaling patient responses to the questions.

name: menu planning
query: Query: menu planning [SEP] Menu planning is a food service control process involving scheduling of meals in advance.

name: mercury poisoning , nervous system
query: Query: mercury poisoning , nervous system [SEP] Nervous system mercury poisoning is neurologic disorders associated with exposure to inorganic and organic forms of mercury. Acute intoxication may be associated with gastrointestinal disturbances, mental status changes, and paraparesis. Chronic exposure to inorganic mercury usually occurs in industrial workers, and manifests as mental confusion, prominent behavioral changes (including psychosis), dyskinesias, and neuritis. Alkyl mercury poisoning may occur through ingestion of contaminated seafood or grain, and its characteristic features include polyneuropathy; ataxia; vision loss; nystagmus, pathologic; and deafness. (From Joynt, Clinical Neurology, 1997, Ch20, pp10-15)

name: metabolic side effects of drugs and substances
query: Query: metabolic side effects of drugs and substances [SEP] Metabolic side effects of drugs and substances is specific effects of drugs and substances on metabolic pathways such as those occurring through the cytochrome p-450 enzyme system. These include effects that often result in drug interactions; food-drug interactions; and herb-drug interactions.

name: metal nanoparticles
query: Query: metal nanoparticles [SEP] Metal nanoparticles is nanoparticles produced from metals whose uses include biosensors, optics, and catalysts. In biomedical applications the particles frequently involve the noble metals, especially gold and silver.

name: mexican americans
query: Query: mexican americans [SEP] Mexican americans is persons living in the United States of Mexican descent.

name: mice , obese
query: Query: mice , obese [SEP] Obese mice is mutant mice exhibiting a marked obesity coupled with overeating, hyperglycemia, hyperinsulinemia, marked insulin resistance, and infertility when in a homozygous state. They may be inbred or hybrid.

name: micelles
query: Query: micelles [SEP] Micelles is particles consisting of aggregates of molecules held loosely together by secondary bonds. The surface of micelles are usually comprised of amphiphatic compounds that are oriented in a way that minimizes the energy of interaction between the micelle and its environment. Liquids that contain large numbers of suspended micelles are referred to as emulsions.

name: microsatellite instability
query: Query: microsatellite instability [SEP] Microsatellite instability is the occurrence of highly polymorphic mono- and dinucleotide microsatellite repeats in somatic cells. It is a form of genome instability associated with defects in dna mismatch repair.

name: microscopy , atomic force
query: Query: microscopy , atomic force [SEP] Atomic force microscopy is a type of scanning probe microscopy in which a probe systematically rides across the surface of a sample being scanned in a raster pattern. The vertical position is recorded as a spring attached to the probe rises and falls in response to peaks and valleys on the surface. These deflections produce a topographic map of the sample.

name: microscopy , video
query: Query: microscopy , video [SEP] Video microscopy is microscopy in which television cameras are used to brighten magnified images that are otherwise too dark to be seen with the naked eye. It is used frequently in telepathology.

name: military science
query: Query: military science [SEP] Military science is study of the causes as well as tactical and strategic principles of warfare.

name: milk , human
query: Query: milk , human [SEP] Human milk is milk that is produced by human mammary glands.

name: milk banks
query: Query: milk banks [SEP] Milk banks is centers for acquiring, storing, and distributing human milk.

name: milk sickness
query: Query: milk sickness [SEP] Milk sickness is an acute, often fatal disease caused by the ingestion of milk, milk products, or the flesh of cattle or sheep which have a disease known as trembles. It is marked by weakness, anorexia, vomiting, constipation, and sometimes muscular tremors. It is caused by poisoning by white snakeroot (Eupatorium rugosum) and the rayless goldenrod (Haplopappus heterophyllus). (From Dorland, 27th ed)

name: mineral waters
query: Query: mineral waters [SEP] Mineral waters is water naturally or artificially infused with mineral salts or gases.

name: minnesota
query: Query: minnesota [SEP] Minnesota is state bordered on the north by Canada, on the east by Lake Superior and Wisconsin, on the south by Iowa, and on the west by North Dakota and South Dakota.

name: minor surgical procedures
query: Query: minor surgical procedures [SEP] Minor surgical procedures is surgery for problems and injuries that are of relatively slight extent, and with a low risk for life threatening complications.

name: mitochondrial dynamics
query: Query: mitochondrial dynamics [SEP] Mitochondrial dynamics is the continuous remodeling of mitochondria shape by fission and fusion in response to physiological conditions.

name: mitochondrial membranes
query: Query: mitochondrial membranes [SEP] Mitochondrial membranes is the two lipoprotein layers in the mitochondrion. The outer membrane encloses the entire mitochondrion and contains channels with transport proteins to move molecules and ions in and out of the organelle. The inner membrane folds into cristae and contains many enzymes important to cell metabolism and energy production (mitochondrial atp synthase).

name: mitotic index
query: Query: mitotic index [SEP] Mitotic index is an expression of the number of mitoses found in a stated number of cells.

name: mitral valve insufficiency
query: Query: mitral valve insufficiency [SEP] Mitral valve insufficiency is backflow of blood from the left ventricle into the left atrium due to imperfect closure of the mitral valve. This can lead to mitral valve regurgitation.

name: models , chemical
query: Query: models , chemical [SEP] Chemical models is theoretical representations that simulate the behavior or activity of chemical processes or phenomena; includes the use of mathematical equations, computers, and other electronic equipment.

name: models , econometric
query: Query: models , econometric [SEP] Econometric models is the application of mathematical formulas and statistical techniques to the testing and quantifying of economic theories and the solution of economic problems.

name: models , educational
query: Query: models , educational [SEP] Educational models is theoretical models which propose methods of learning or teaching as a basis or adjunct to changes in attitude or behavior. These educational interventions are usually applied in the fields of health and patient education but are not restricted to patient care.

name: models , psychological
query: Query: models , psychological [SEP] Psychological models is theoretical representations that simulate psychological processes and/or social processes. These include the use of mathematical equations, computers, and other electronic equipment.

name: molecular sequence annotation
query: Query: molecular sequence annotation [SEP] Molecular sequence annotation is the addition of descriptive information about the function or structure of a molecular sequence to its molecular sequence data record.

name: moral status
query: Query: moral status [SEP] Moral status is a philosophical description of intrinsic self-worth and dignity which bestows basic rights of life, liberty, and freedom from harm.

name: morphine
query: Query: morphine [SEP] Morphine is the principal alkaloid in opium and the prototype opiate analgesic and narcotic. Morphine has widespread effects in the central nervous system and on smooth muscle.

name: moscow
query: Query: moscow [SEP] Moscow is the capital of Russia.

name: mosquito nets
query: Query: mosquito nets [SEP] Mosquito nets is free-standing or supported lightweight meshwork fabric made of cotton, silk, polyester or other material, having openings too small to allow entry of mosquitoes or other insects, thereby protecting against insect bites; insect stings, and insect-borne diseases.

name: multiple organ failure
query: Query: multiple organ failure [SEP] Multiple organ failure is a progressive condition usually characterized by combined failure of several organs such as the lungs, liver, kidney, along with some clotting mechanisms, usually postinjury or postoperative.

name: multiple sclerosis , chronic progressive
query: Query: multiple sclerosis , chronic progressive [SEP] Chronic progressive multiple sclerosis is a form of multiple sclerosis characterized by a progressive deterioration in neurologic function which is in contrast to the more typical relapsing remitting form. If the clinical course is free of distinct remissions, it is referred to as primary progressive multiple sclerosis. When the progressive decline is punctuated by acute exacerbations, it is referred to as progressive relapsing multiple sclerosis. The term secondary progressive multiple sclerosis is used when relapsing remitting multiple sclerosis evolves into the chronic progressive form. (From Ann Neurol 1994;36 Suppl:S73-S79; Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, pp903-914)

name: multiple system atrophy
query: Query: multiple system atrophy [SEP] Multiple system atrophy is a syndrome complex composed of three conditions which represent clinical variants of the same disease process: striatonigral degeneration; shy-drager syndrome; and the sporadic form of olivopontocerebellar atrophies. Clinical features include autonomic, cerebellar, and basal ganglia dysfunction. Pathologic examination reveals atrophy of the basal ganglia, cerebellum, pons, and medulla, with prominent loss of autonomic neurons in the brain stem and spinal cord. (From Adams et al., Principles of Neurology, 6th ed, p1076; Baillieres Clin Neurol 1997 Apr;6(1):187-204; Med Clin North Am 1999 Mar;83(2):381-92)

name: mycobacterium tuberculosis
query: Query: mycobacterium tuberculosis [SEP] Mycobacterium tuberculosis is a species of gram-positive, aerobic bacteria that produces tuberculosis in humans, other primates, cattle; dogs; and some other animals which have contact with humans. Growth tends to be in serpentine, cordlike masses in which the bacilli show a parallel orientation.

name: myocardial contraction
query: Query: myocardial contraction [SEP] Myocardial contraction is contractile activity of the myocardium.

name: myocardial perfusion imaging
query: Query: myocardial perfusion imaging [SEP] Myocardial perfusion imaging is the creation and display of functional images showing where the blood is flowing into the myocardium by following over time the distribution of tracers injected into the blood stream.

name: myocytes , cardiac
query: Query: myocytes , cardiac [SEP] Cardiac myocytes is striated muscle cells found in the heart. They are derived from cardiac myoblasts (myoblasts, cardiac).

name: nanotechnology
query: Query: nanotechnology [SEP] Nanotechnology is the development and use of techniques to study physical phenomena and construct structures in the nanoscale size range or smaller.

name: nasal lavage fluid
query: Query: nasal lavage fluid [SEP] Nasal lavage fluid is fluid obtained by therapeutic irrigation or washout of the nasal cavity and nasal mucosa. The resulting fluid is used in cytologic and immunologic assays of the nasal mucosa such as with the nasal provocation test in the diagnosis of nasal hypersensitivity.

name: nasal polyps
query: Query: nasal polyps [SEP] Nasal polyps is focal accumulations of edema fluid in the nasal mucosa accompanied by hyperplasia of the associated submucosal connective tissue. Polyps may be neoplasms, foci of inflammation, degenerative lesions, or malformations.

name: natural cytotoxicity triggering receptor 1
query: Query: natural cytotoxicity triggering receptor 1 [SEP] Natural cytotoxicity triggering receptor 1 is a 46-kD stimulatory receptor found on resting and activated natural killer cells. It has specificity for viral hemagglutinins that are expressed on infected cells.

name: natural cytotoxicity triggering receptor 2
query: Query: natural cytotoxicity triggering receptor 2 [SEP] Natural cytotoxicity triggering receptor 2 is a 44-kD stimulatory receptor found on activated natural killer cells. It has specificity for viral hemagglutinins that are expressed on infected cells.

name: natural language processing
query: Query: natural language processing [SEP] Natural language processing is computer processing of a language with rules that reflect and describe current usage rather than prescribed usage.

name: neck
query: Query: neck [SEP] Neck is the part of a human or animal body connecting the head to the rest of the body.

name: negative staining
query: Query: negative staining [SEP] Negative staining is the technique of washing tissue specimens with a concentrated solution of a heavy metal salt and letting it dry. The specimen will be covered with a very thin layer of the metal salt, being excluded in areas where an adsorbed macromolecule is present. The macromolecules allow electrons from the beam of an electron microscope to pass much more readily than the heavy metal; thus, a reversed or negative image of the molecule is created.

name: neonatal nursing
query: Query: neonatal nursing [SEP] Neonatal nursing is the nursing specialty that deals with the care of newborn infants during the first four weeks after birth.

name: neonatal sepsis
query: Query: neonatal sepsis [SEP] Neonatal sepsis is blood infection that occurs in an infant younger than 90 days old. Early-onset sepsis is seen in the first week of life and most often appears within 24 hours of birth. Late-onset occurs after 1 week and before 3 months of age.

name: neoplasm staging
query: Query: neoplasm staging [SEP] Neoplasm staging is methods which attempt to express in replicable terms the extent of the neoplasm in the patient.

name: nervous system autoimmune disease , experimental
query: Query: nervous system autoimmune disease , experimental [SEP] Experimental nervous system autoimmune disease is experimental animal models for human autoimmune diseases of the nervous system. They include guillain-barre syndrome (see neuritis, autoimmune, experimental); myasthenia gravis (see myasthenia gravis, autoimmune, experimental); and multiple sclerosis (see encephalomyelitis, autoimmune, experimental).

name: nested genes
query: Query: nested genes [SEP] Nested genes is genes whose entire sequences are contained within other genes.

name: neural tube defects
query: Query: neural tube defects [SEP] Neural tube defects is congenital malformations of the central nervous system and adjacent structures related to defective neural tube closure during the first trimester of pregnancy generally occurring between days 18-29 of gestation. Ectodermal and mesodermal malformations (mainly involving the skull and vertebrae) may occur as a result of defects of neural tube closure. (From Joynt, Clinical Neurology, 1992, Ch55, pp31-41)

name: neuromuscular blocking agents
query: Query: neuromuscular blocking agents [SEP] Neuromuscular blocking agents is drugs that interrupt transmission of nerve impulses at the skeletal neuromuscular junction. They can be of two types, competitive, stabilizing blockers (neuromuscular nondepolarizing agents) or noncompetitive, depolarizing agents (neuromuscular depolarizing agents). Both prevent acetylcholine from triggering the muscle contraction and they are used as anesthesia adjuvants, as relaxants during electroshock, in convulsive states, etc.

name: new zealand
query: Query: new zealand [SEP] New zealand is a group of islands in the southwest Pacific. Its capital is Wellington. It was discovered by the Dutch explorer Abel Tasman in 1642 and circumnavigated by Cook in 1769. Colonized in 1840 by the New Zealand Company, it became a British crown colony in 1840 until 1907 when colonial status was terminated. New Zealand is a partly anglicized form of the original Dutch name Nieuw Zeeland, new sea land, possibly with reference to the Dutch province of Zeeland. (From Webster's New Geographical Dictionary, 1988, p842 & Room, Brewer's Dictionary of Names, 1992, p378)

name: night care
query: Query: night care [SEP] Night care is institutional night care of patients.

name: night eating syndrome
query: Query: night eating syndrome [SEP] Night eating syndrome is little or no appetite for breakfast due to eating more food after dinner than during the meal and eating more than half of daily food intake after dinner hour.

name: night vision
query: Query: night vision [SEP] Night vision is function of the human eye that is used in dim illumination (scotopic intensities) or at nighttime. Scotopic vision is performed by retinal rod photoreceptors with high sensitivity to light and peak absorption wavelength at 507 nm near the blue end of the spectrum.

name: nodal protein
query: Query: nodal protein [SEP] Nodal protein is the founding member of the nodal signaling ligand family of proteins. Nodal protein was originally discovered in the region of the mouse embryo primitive streak referred to as hensen's node. It is expressed asymmetrically on the left side in chordates and plays a critical role in the genesis of left-right asymmetry during vertebrate development.

name: noninvasive ventilation
query: Query: noninvasive ventilation [SEP] Noninvasive ventilation is techniques for administering artificial respiration without the need for intratracheal intubation.

name: nonlinear dynamics
query: Query: nonlinear dynamics [SEP] Nonlinear dynamics is the study of systems which respond disproportionately (nonlinearly) to initial conditions or perturbing stimuli. Nonlinear systems may exhibit "chaos" which is classically characterized as sensitive dependence on initial conditions. Chaotic systems, while distinguished from more ordered periodic systems, are not random. When their behavior over time is appropriately displayed (in "phase space"), constraints are evident which are described by "strange attractors". Phase space representations of chaotic systems, or strange attractors, usually reveal fractal (fractals) self-similarity across time scales. Natural, including biological, systems often display nonlinear dynamics and chaos.

name: northern ireland
query: Query: northern ireland [SEP] Northern ireland is the northern one-sixth of the island of Ireland - between the North Atlantic Ocean and the North Sea; northwest of France. The capital is Belfast.

name: northern territory
query: Query: northern territory [SEP] Northern territory is territory in north central Australia, between the states of Queensland and Western Australia. Its capital is Darwin.

name: north sea
query: Query: north sea [SEP] North sea is an arm of the Atlantic Ocean extending between Europe on the south and east, Great Britain on the west.

name: nuclear fission
query: Query: nuclear fission [SEP] Nuclear fission is nuclear reaction in which the nucleus of a heavy atom such as uranium or plutonium is split into two approximately equal parts by a neutron, charged particle, or photon.

name: nuclear localization signals
query: Query: nuclear localization signals [SEP] Nuclear localization signals is short, predominantly basic amino acid sequences identified as nuclear import signals for some proteins. These sequences are believed to interact with specific receptors at the nuclear pore.

name: nuclear medicine department , hospital

name: nuclear pharmacy

name: nursing informatics

name: nutritional requirements

name: nutritional status
query: Query: nutritional status [SEP] Nutritional status is state of the body in relation to the consumption and utilization of nutrients.

name: occupational dentistry

name: occupational therapy
query: Query: occupational therapy [SEP] Occupational therapy is skilled treatment that helps individuals achieve independence in all facets of their lives. It assists in the development of skills needed for independent living.

name: office nursing
query: Query: office nursing [SEP] Office nursing is nursing practice limited to an office setting.

name: oil and gas industry
query: Query: oil and gas industry [SEP] Oil and gas industry is industry concerned with the extraction, processing, distribution, marketing and storage of petroleum and natural gas.

name: olfactory receptor neurons

Their unmyelinated axons synapse in the olfactory bulb of the brain.

Conventional labels for the probe include the radioisotope labels 32p and 125i and the chemical label biotin.

name: olive oil
query: Query: olive oil [SEP] Olive oil is oil extracted from fruit of the olive tree (genus Olea).

name: oncogene addiction

name: oncogene proteins , fusion

name: oncology service , hospital

name: operating room information systems
query: Query: operating room information systems [SEP] Operating room information systems is information systems, usually computer-assisted, designed to store, manipulate, and retrieve information for planning, organizing, directing, and controlling administrative activities associated with the provision and utilization of operating room services and facilities.

name: ophthalmic artery
query: Query: ophthalmic artery [SEP] Ophthalmic artery is artery originating from the internal carotid artery and distributing to the eye, orbit and adjacent facial structures.

name: ophthalmic assistants

name: opportunistic infections
query: Query: opportunistic infections [SEP] Opportunistic infections is an infection caused by an organism which becomes pathogenic under certain conditions, e.g., during immunosuppression.

name: optic atrophy , autosomal dominant
query: Query: optic atrophy , autosomal dominant [SEP] Autosomal dominant optic atrophy is dominant optic atrophy is a hereditary optic neuropathy causing decreased visual acuity, color vision deficits, a centrocecal scotoma, and optic nerve pallor (Hum. Genet. 1998; 102: 79-86). Mutations leading to this condition have been mapped to the opa1 gene at chromosome 3q28-q29. opa1 codes for a dynamin-related GTPase that localizes to mitochondria.

name: optic disk
query: Query: optic disk [SEP] Optic disk is the portion of the optic nerve seen in the fundus with the ophthalmoscope. It is formed by the meeting of all the retinal ganglion cell axons as they enter the optic nerve.

name: oral health
query: Query: oral health [SEP] Oral health is the optimal state of the mouth and normal functioning of the organs of the mouth without evidence of disease.

name: oral medicine
query: Query: oral medicine [SEP] Oral medicine is a branch of dentistry dealing with diseases of the oral and paraoral structures and the oral management of systemic diseases. (Hall, What is Oral Medicine, Anyway? Clinical Update: National Naval Dental Center, March 1991, p7-8)

name: orbit
query: Query: orbit [SEP] Orbit is bony cavity that holds the eyeball and its associated tissues and appendages.

name: orbital neoplasms
query: Query: orbital neoplasms [SEP] Orbital neoplasms is neoplasms of the bony orbit and contents except the eyeball.

name: organic cation transporter 1

name: organic cation transporter 2
query: Query: organic cation transporter 2 [SEP] Organic cation transporter 2 is organic cation transporter consisting of twelve transmembrane domains and expressed primarily in the kidney. name: organizational case studies
query: Query: organizational case studies [SEP] Organizational case studies is descriptions and evaluations of specific health care organizations.

name: organizational policy
query: Query: organizational policy [SEP] Organizational policy is a course or method of action selected, usually by an organization, institution, university, society, etc., from among alternatives to guide and determine present and future decisions and positions on matters of public interest or social concern. name: orientation , spatial
query: Query: orientation , spatial [SEP] Spatial orientation is change in position or alignment in response to an external stimulus.

name: orthodontic brackets
query: Query: orthodontic brackets [SEP] Orthodontic brackets is small metal or ceramic attachments used to fasten an arch wire.
